Vision & Strategy

  • Own and articulate the long-term product vision for Keet as the world's leading private, peer-to-peer communication app, with a clear path to 1 billion users.

  • Analyze WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, LINE, WeChat and emerging competitors to identify where P2P gives Keet an unfair advantage, and build the roadmap around it.

  • Present product vision, strategy, metrics and progress to the board and executive leadership with clarity and conviction.

Define a growth strategy across acquisition, activation, retention and virality, with measurable targets at every stage.

Technical Product Leadership

  • Develop a deep working understanding of the Holepunch P2P stack (Pear runtime, Bare, Hypercore, Hyperswarm, HyperDHT, Autobase, Hyperbee) and translate its capabilities and constraints into product decisions.

  • Partner with core engineering on hard P2P problems at scale, including NAT traversal, offline sync, multi-device support, large groups, push notifications, and battery and data efficiency on mobile.

  • Own the real-time calling experience (1:1 and group voice and video, plus screen sharing) to a quality bar that matches or beats Google Meet and Zoom.

  • Define clear feature tiers with explicit labels for stable versus experimental functionality.

Rapid Prototyping with AI

  • Use AI coding and design tools to build working prototypes and demos that prove concepts before committing engineering resources.

  • Turn ideas into something the team, users and the board can see and touch within days.

Execution & Team Leadership

  • Lead the product team and run the sprint cadence end to end, covering planning, prioritization, standups, reviews and retrospectives.

  • Own deliverables from conception through release, testing and post-launch iteration, ensuring core functionality works reliably every time.

  • Maintain issue trackers and roadmaps that accurately reflect priorities and sprint commitments.

  • Coordinate across engineering, QA, design, marketing and business stakeholders, and manage cross-team dependencies across the Holepunch and Tether ecosystem.

  • Provide transparent updates on status, risks and timeline changes, and hold direct conversations about accountability when needed.

  • Own the mobile release process across iOS and Android. This includes App Store and Google Play submissions, review guidelines, compliance, store listings, ratings and release management.

Role Overview:

The Vocational Rehabilitation Specialist is a frontline professional resource within the Vocational Services Department who applies accredited rehabilitation counseling expertise to support absence management and disability insurance services delivered under employer-based group benefit policies and contracts. This role provides vocational, occupational, and workplace accommodation expertise across multiple functional areas, including Pre-Disability and ADA accommodations, Short-Term and Long-Term Disability return-to-work services, vocational analyses and reporting, and participation in live claim staffings.

The position is designed as a hybrid role. While individual work assignments may emphasize specific functional areas at different times, the Vocational Rehabilitation Specialist is expected to maintain the knowledge, skills, and competencies necessary to support all core Vocational Services functions. The role does not adjudicate or pay claims. Instead, it delivers expert vocational input, analysis, and customer-facing services that claims professionals and employer partners use to inform benefit decisions and support safe, productive work outcomes.

This role requires in-depth practical expertise, independent problem-solving, sound professional judgment, and the ability to serve as a reliable vocational resource for internal and external clients, partners, and customers.

Vocational Expertise and Analysis

Return-to-Work and Stay-at-Work Services

ADA, Pre-Disability, and Workplace Accommodation Support

Live Claim Staffing and Collaboration

  • Participate in live claim staffings and consultations with claims managers, nurses, behavioral health professionals, and other partners.
  • Provide real-time vocational input related to occupational demands, work capacity, accommodation feasibility, and return-to-work planning.
  • Serve as a subject matter resource, explaining vocational concepts, industry practices, and labor market considerations in a clear and practical manner.
    •

Collaboration, Quality, and Continuous Improvement

  • Work independently while collaborating closely with vocational peers, claims teams, and other internal partners to deliver consistent, high-quality services.
  • Apply established best practices, procedures, and quality standards across all functional areas.
  • Identify trends, issues, or opportunities for improvement and share observations with team leaders or senior vocational staff.
  • Participate in training, onboarding, calibration, and professional development activities.

Preferred

  • Experience completing own occupation analyses and transferable skills analyses in a disability insurance environment.
  • Additional relevant licenses or certifications (e.g., LPC, CVE, CCM, CDMS, CEAS).
  • Experience providing job retention, stay-at-work, or return-to-work services within group disability or absence management programs.
  • Experience working within a Continuous Improvement (CI) Management System, including application of the core CI disciplines of connecting work to strategy and customer value, discovering better ways of working, delivering value efficiently, and enabling people to contribute to their fullest potential. Preferred experience includes participating as a frontline contributor in CI practices such as standard work, visual management, demand and capacity discussions, problem-solving, and performance conversations, and using CI tools to build behaviors that support quality, transparency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (Backend, AI)
jobs.excerpt: Teach AI to understand a company's revenue data, so marketers stop waiting for engineers.
jobs.description:
Teach AI to understand a company's revenue data, so marketers stop waiting for engineers.

At N.Rich, agents write most of the code. Engineers lead the agents and own the judgement: what to build, what not to build, and whether the answer is correct.

About N.Rich

N.Rich is the buildable ABM platform for B2B revenue teams. We find the accounts showing buying intent, put ads in front of them through our own DSP, and show sales when to move. More than 250 go-to-market teams use N.Rich, including GE HealthCare, JetBrains and Wärtsilä. We were founded in Helsinki in 2015.

Our newest product, N.Rich AI, is now the centre of the company. Teams describe what they need in plain language, and N.Rich AI builds a live app on their own data and acts on it.

  • One set of numbers: a governed data layer joins CRM, website, LinkedIn and ad data, so every app gives the same answer.

  • Proof of impact: it shows which programmes and channels created pipeline, reconciled to the customer's own reports.

  • Action: accounts an app finds become ad audiences or Salesforce and HubSpot lists, and results flow back in.

Why now

  • N.Rich AI solves the problem others avoid. Competitors use AI for small things, like more ad variations. N.Rich AI shows what marketing did for revenue, on numbers finance trusts.

  • The next few quarters decide the category. A lead like ours does not last forever. What you ship in your first months goes straight to customers.

  • We are opening the product up. Anyone can now try N.Rich AI without a sales call. Builders who share apps on it can join our partner programme. Every shared app brings in the next user.

  • We ship fast. The N.Rich AI playground went from idea on 17 September to a beta in production a month later. On 10 September the team said AI apps couldn't move between our EU and US regions. One week later, one-click transfer was live, with design and review.

Problems you will work on

  1. A semantic layer on clients' CRM data. Build it on top of clients' Salesforce and HubSpot data, so AI understands their business and can answer real questions about it.

  2. Our own AI harness for revenue teams. Marketers and sales people do things on their own that needed engineers before.

  3. Who is behind a website visit. Identify the people behind website visits with our own algorithms, on top of the data we already have.

How we work

Everyone at N.Rich works through their own AI system, not just engineers. We pay for models and tools from more than one provider, so you can experiment freely and use what fits each task best. Our team works from 20+ countries. You join an R&D team of 17 people (8 developers, 3 data scientists, QA, DevOps and design) and report to Anton, our CTO. You work closely with product and revenue.

You will fit if you

  • Have shipped projects that run in production with real users and real problems, and owned them from the goal to production.

  • Work every day through your own AI setup: agents connected to your tools, a model from another provider reviewing their work, repeated work turned into skills. For Tech lead, agents also keep working in the background. You will show it to us live.

  • Make technical decisions that still hold a year later, including "let's not build this".

  • Spot problems early, in or outside your area, and bring a fix.

  • Care who the work is for, and talk to product and revenue to find out.

You probably already have: 5+ years as a software engineer, strong experience in one popular language (TypeScript, Java or Python), SQL and relational databases, APIs, distributed systems basics, Docker and CI/CD, fluent English.

A bonus, not a must: agents, MCP servers or skills others use; LLM-based products; data and analytics platforms; marketing or ad tech; Salesforce or HubSpot integrations; event-driven systems.

This is not for you if you

  • Can't make decisions on your own.

  • Need a fixed roadmap and stable priorities.

  • Aren't ready to change fast.

  • Don't want to talk to clients.

What we expect from each other

Four values guide how we work. We call them C.O.R.E., and we hire, give feedback and grow against them.

  • Context & System Thinking. Know why the work matters before you start. Understand who it's for and what else it touches.

  • Ownership. Own the outcome, not the task. Raise risks early and take responsibility for the result, not the handoff.

  • Radical Candor. Challenge ideas directly and assume good intent. We keep problems small by talking about them early.

  • Execution at Scale. Be the lead engineer of your own agentic team. Frame the problem so software can solve it, ship the smallest useful version, check the result, and improve the system so it handles the problem next time.

From the team

  • "Join us to be on the frontier of the AI change instead of watching it from the sidelines. At N.Rich we expect everyone to become an engineer, and R&D is at the center of it." (Anton, CTO)

  • "What's different here is that we leverage AI at every step of building N.Rich AI, and engineers are responsible for the outcome. You decide how to solve the problem and take a feature all the way to production, with people who challenge ideas openly and care about the result." (Oleksiy, Senior Software Engineer)

Pay and terms

Per month. This is a contractor role. We place you in the range based on what you show us when we get to know each other.

  • Senior: up to €7,500 per month

  • Tech lead: up to €10,000 per month

You can work from anywhere within about 2 hours of CET. We can't contract in every country, so we confirm your location in the first talk. We pay for the tools you need to do the work, including AI models from more than one provider, so you pick what works best.

How we get to know each other

No take-home tasks. Apply with your CV or your LinkedIn profile.

  1. Intro call. A short call with our HR Director to get to know each other.

  2. Values conversation. How you work, talked through against our C.O.R.E. values.

  3. Technical prescreen. 30 minutes with Anton, our CTO.

  4. Technical interview. 2 hours. A technical task from our domain, worked through live on the call.

  5. Final talk with Anton. Only if we need it after the earlier steps.

In the application we ask one question: describe your AI setup. What does it connect to, who reviews the agents' work and how, and what are your main learnings?

Poznaj Onwelo

Onwelo jest partnerem technologicznym, który dostarcza kompleksowe usługi, od strategii i architektury, przez wdrożenia, po utrzymanie, w obszarach transformacji cyfrowej, danych i automatyzacji. Kogo szukamy

  • Samodzielność, komunikatywność oraz analityczne podejście do rozwiązywania problemów

  • Bardzo dobra znajomość języka polskiego i angielskiego

Co oferujemy

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Senior Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Analyst

Partner with Leaders. Drive Strategy. Make an Impact.

RS&H is seeking a Senior Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) Analyst to join our Finance team. In this highly visible role, you'll serve as the primary finance partner for Corporate Shared Services, leading budgeting, forecasting, executive financial reporting, and strategic financial planning across the firm. You'll work closely with executive leadership and department leaders to deliver insights that drive informed business decisions.

As a 100% employee-owned architecture, engineering, and consulting firm, RS&H offers the opportunity to build a rewarding career while contributing to the success of a nationally recognized organization.

What You'll Do

  • Lead the annual budgeting process for Corporate Shared Services and G&A functions, coordinating the bottom-up budget build with department leaders, managing timelines, consolidating submissions, and resolving budget gaps.
  • Lead the monthly rolling forecast process, partnering with cost center owners to validate assumptions, maintain accurate forecasts, and support proactive financial planning.
  • Perform variance analysis by interpreting historical trends, developing forward-looking cost projections, and identifying financial risks and opportunities with actionable recommendations.
  • Prepare executive financial reporting packages and facilitate monthly financial reviews with executive stakeholders to discuss business performance, forecast updates, and future outlook.
  • Develop financial models that support workforce planning, operational initiatives, investment decisions, and long-range planning.
  • Serve as a trusted finance partner to business leaders by building strong relationships, providing financial guidance, and supporting strategic decision-making.
  • Develop dashboards and reporting that provide actionable business insights while leveraging AI-assisted tools to improve reporting efficiency and financial analysis.
  • Drive continuous improvement in budgeting, forecasting, and reporting processes to enhance financial planning and operational decision-making.
  • Support enterprise initiatives and special projects by partnering with business leaders to provide financial guidance, strengthen accountability, and evaluate strategic investments.

What You Bring

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field
  • Approximately 5–8+ years of progressive FP&A, corporate finance, or budgeting experience
  • Experience leading annual budgets and rolling forecasts across multiple departments or cost centers
  • Advanced Excel skills, including financial modeling and scenario analysis
  • Experience with Power BI or similar business intelligence and reporting tools
  • Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to partner effectively with senior leaders
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and build strong cross-functional relationships

Preferred Qualifications

  • MBA, CPA, or CFA
  • Experience in the AEC industry or another professional services environment
  • Deltek Vantagepoint, Oracle, SQL, or similar ERP/database experience
  • Experience leveraging AI-enabled tools to improve reporting or analytical workflows

Why RS&H?

At RS&H, you'll join a collaborative, employee-owned firm where your work directly contributes to the success of the business. We offer competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, professional development opportunities, and a culture built on collaboration, innovation, and shared success.

Join RS&H and help create tomorrow, together.

Typical salary range for this position will commensurate with experience relative to the position and will be at the ranges included below for each location:

Richmond and Virginia Beach, VA – 100,000 – 159,000 

Denver, CO – 106,000 - 169,000

Vienna, VA and Baltimore, MD is $115,000 – 180,000

**Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a permanent basis. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship or visa transfer.**

An Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

Please view Equal Employment Opportunity Posters provided by OFCCP here.

Please note: no agency representation or submissions will be recognized for this vacancy. Candidates should apply directly to this role to be considered. It is the responsibility of all third-party recruiting and employment agencies to know and adhere to our recruiting policy.

The Company

Employee-owned, RS&H is one of the nation’s leading architecture, engineering, and consulting firms, with associates who work hard every day to create tomorrow together. We offer an exceptional journey from start to future. Our integrated teams translate experience into insight, turn challenges into opportunities, and build relationships that are as strong as the buildings and infrastructure we deliver together. We attribute our success to our unwavering commitment to our core values: integrity, accountability, curiosity, and teamwork.

jobs.title: SEO & Content Writing Specialist
jobs.excerpt: SUMMARY The Search Engine Optimization (SEO) Specialist supports the execution of the organization's search engine optimization strategy to increase online visibility, drive qualified organic traffic, and improve overall website performance.
jobs.description:
SUMMARY

The Search Engine Optimization (SEO) Specialist supports the execution of the organization's search engine optimization strategy to increase online visibility, drive qualified organic traffic, and improve overall website performance. Reporting to Director of SEO this role is hands-on and focused on Search and AI discoverability while creating a positive user and client experience across the website. The SEO partners with the PR team on SEO-related media outreach and link building efforts, as well as the broader marketing team to ensure SEO best practices are consistently applied, while contributing insights that inform strategy and drive measurable growth.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Conduct keyword research, competitor analysis, and site audits to identify opportunities for new content or additional SEO/AEO optimization. Implement on-page optimizations including title tags, meta descriptions, header tags, internal linking, and schema markup. Develop content optimization efforts across landing pages, blogs, and multimedia assets to improve visibility and engagement. Research, write and optimize clear, user-focused website copy and though leadership for B2B audiences. Use keyword and performance data, along with an understanding of ICPs/personas and the buyer journey, to address audience needs at each stage and improve visibility in traditional search and AI engines. Partner with subject matter experts to develop accurate, useful content, translating their expertise into clear copy aligned with audience needs, search intent, and business goals. Assist in the creation and management of SEO and Search Engine Marketing (SEM) campaigns across platforms. Track, measure, and report on SEO KPIs such as rankings, traffic, engagement, and conversions. Surface actionable insights to the Director based on trend analysis. Utilize tools such as GA4, GSC, BrightEdge to monitor performance and surface insights. Maintain dashboards and reporting accuracy across SEO and paid channels. Stay current on search engine algorithm updates, SEO trends, and emerging tools. Experiment with new tactics, including generative AI-driven search and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), under the guidance of the Director of SEO. Contribute ideas to improve processes, tools, and outcomes for SEO initiatives. Partner with manager and broader marketing team to ensure SEO is integrated into all digital projects. Support campaign planning, execution, and reporting to align with business goals. Assist in testing landing page templates, modules, and content variations to optimize user experience and search performance.

QUALIFICATIONS

EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field , or equivalent combination of education and experience Three (3) or more years of experience in SEO or digital marketing with a proven track record of improving website rankings and traffic. Three (3) or more years of content writing experience, preferably in a B2B environment

SKILLS

Knowledge of on-page optimization (title tags, meta descriptions, internal linking, schema markup) Proficiency with SEO tools such as Google Search Console, Google Analytics (GA4), BrightEdge, SEMrush, Ahrefs, Moz or equivalent Knowledge of technical SEO (site speed, mobile optimization, crawlability, Core Web Vitals) Detail-oriented and able to manage multiple projects simultaneously Strong written and verbal communication skills

jobs.title: Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) Senior Adviser – South
jobs.excerpt: With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life.
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

Local - Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:


JOB PURPOSE

Provide strategic and technical leadership to advance gender equality, disability inclusion and social inclusion across the South Asia and Pacific region. The role develops and delivers a regional GEDSI roadmap; strengthens organisational practice and staff and partner capability; embeds GEDSI across strategy, programme and proposal design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning; and positions World Vision with donors, governments, UN agencies, civil society and representative organisations.


Core areas of focus:

  • Develop and execute a regional GEDSI strategy and roadmap aligned with organisational policy and child well-being priorities.
  • Lead GEDSI mainstreaming and quality assurance across regional and national office programming, grants and organisational systems.
  • Build the capability of GEDSI focal points, technical teams, leaders, partners and representative organisations.
  • Generate evidence, learning, innovation and external positioning on GEDSI across development, humanitarian and fragile contexts.
  • Manage and coordinate GEDSI-related consultancies, technical assistance engagements, and partnerships, including development of scopes of work, procurement inputs, onboarding, quality assurance, delivery oversight, and dissemination of outputs to ensure alignment with global and regional priorities and standards.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


Lead regional GEDSI strategy, policy implementation and organizational change.

  • Develop and monitor a regional GEDSI strategy and roadmap aligned with organizational priorities and policy.
  • Engage regional and national leadership, People & Culture, operations, programmes, grants, advocacy and communications to embed GEDSI in programming, organizational practices, advocacy and external engagement, and in communications, as per World Vision’s GEDSI Policy.
  • Guide organizational GEDSI self-assessments and action plans; promote inclusive language, accessible workplaces, non-discrimination and reasonable accommodation.
  • Ensure GEDSI is visible in organizational priorities,program strategies and design, key messages andresource allocation.

Lead GEDSI mainstreaming in programs, implementation and proposals across funding streams.

  • Provide technical leadership for GEDSI responsive and transformative programme and proposal design across sectors and contexts.
  • Ensure designs are informed by GEDSI analysis, including gender and disability analysis, barriers, disparities, harmful norms, root causes and intersectional risks.
  • Advise teams on GEDSI objectives, theories of change, indicators, budgets, risk mitigation, Do No Harm, safeguarding and donor requirements.
  • Contextualize and promote GEDSI tools, approaches, minimum standards, domains of change, continuum and marker.
  • Strengthen identification and use of disaggregated data, including appropriate use of Washington Group Questions or other approved tools, informing program / project designs based on analysis.
  • Coach teams to monitor emerging barriers and adapt implementation to improve equitable access, participation, decision-making, systems and well-being.
  • Promote rights-based and social-model approaches that address attitudinal, environmental, communication and institutional barriers.

Build GEDSI capability, networks and communities of practice.

  • Assess competency and capacity gaps and develop regional capacity-strengthening plans for staff, focal points, partners and leaders.
  • Deliver and coordinate contextualised training, coaching, mentoring and peer learning on gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion and related frameworks.
  • Empower GEDSI focal points and technical teams with tools, models, resources and quality assurance support.
  • Strengthen regional collaboration networks and communities of practice, including linkages with gender equality and disability inclusion leadership networks.

Lead evidence, learning, innovation and knowledge management.

  • Develop and implement a regional GEDSI learning agenda linked to child well-being outcomes.
  • Initiate and oversee research, pilots and testing of new or adapted GEDSI approaches and programming models.
  • Support analysis and use of data, evaluations, learning reviews, impact stories, case studies and promising practices.
  • Facilitate knowledge sharing across national offices, the wider Partnership and external audiences.

Build strategic partnerships, external positioning and thought leadership.

  • Represent and position World Vision with governments, donors, UN agencies, clusters, working groups, NGOs, faith actors, academia and regional networks.
  • Build or increase capacity to build strategic and equitable partnerships with women-led organizations, organizations of persons with disabilities and minority groups as part of social inclusion, including children, to ensure that they participate meaningfully in assessment, design, implementation, monitoring, learning and advocacy.
  • Identify opportunities for shared learning, advocacy, policy influence, resource mobilization and thought leadership.
  • Support communications and external engagement colleagues to use inclusive, rights based and evidence-informed GEDSI language and narratives.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILL AND EXPERIENCE

  • Master’s degree or equivalent in gender studies, disability studies, social or political sciences, social work, international development, economics, public policy, programme management or a related field. A bachelor’s degree with substantial relevant experience may be considered.
  • Relevant professional development in gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, safeguarding, programme design, MEAL or humanitarian programming.
  • Minimum 7 years of demonstrated experience providing strategic and technical leadership on gender equality, disability inclusion and social inclusion in international development and/or humanitarian programming.
  • Experience supporting GEDSI-responsive and transformative designs, mainstreaming strategies and activities across multiple sectors and funding streams.
  • Experience leading GEDSI analysis, including gender and disability analysis, and integrating findings into design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and learning.
  • Substantial experience in disability-inclusive programming, accessibility, disability disaggregated data, partnership with organisations of persons with disabilities, and rights-based approaches.
  • Strong facilitation, coaching, relationship-building, partnership, influencing, writing and presentation skills.
  • Experience in organisational change, policy implementation, advocacy, research, knowledge management, external engagement and donor positioning.
  • Experience leading or supporting organisational GEDSI self-assessments, audits or action plans and building the capability of staff and partners.
  • Experience applying Do No Harm, safeguarding and ethical approaches to gender-based violence and other GEDSI-related risks.

Required Language: English


Required travel and/or work environment accommodations: Approximately 30%, subject to operational needs


Preferred Experience, Knowledge and/or other Qualifications:

  • Detailed knowledge of current gender equality, disability inclusion and broader social inclusion approaches in development, humanitarian and fragile contexts.
  • Knowledge of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, CEDAW, the Convention on the Rights of the Child and relevant donor frameworks and markers.
  • Ability to connect GEDSI programming and organisational change to child well-being outcomes.
  • Ability to analyse and communicate disaggregated evidence, identify barriers and root causes, and translate findings into practical programme, policy and budget recommendations.
  • Experience working in or across the South Asia and Pacific region and adapting global approaches to diverse national and local contexts.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Personal Client Manager is responsible for managing and servicing a sophisticated portfolio of affluent and high net worth personal insurance clients. This position serves as a trusted insurance resource to clients and works closely with Risk Advisors, insurance carriers, and internal service team members to identify exposures, develop comprehensive coverage solutions, and deliver an exceptional client experience.The position is responsible for maintaining strong client relationships, coordinating the renewal and marketing process, identifying coverage gaps and opportunities, and ensuring accounts are serviced accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with agency standards.

Essential Functions
Client Relationship & Account Management
  • Manage and service a portfolio of high net worth and affluent personal lines clients, providing a high level of responsiveness, professionalism, and personalized attention.
  • Serve as a primary day-to-day contact for clients regarding coverage questions, policy changes, billing matters, claims assistance, renewal planning, and other insurance needs.
  • Develop a detailed understanding of each client's assets, lifestyle, risk profile, family circumstances, and insurance priorities to provide appropriate recommendations.
  • Build trusted, long-term client relationships by providing proactive guidance and anticipating needs rather than relying solely on client-initiated requests.
  • Maintain a high degree of professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality when handling sensitive client and financial information.

Coverage Analysis & Risk Management

  • Review personal insurance programs and identify potential coverage gaps, overlaps, limits concerns, and opportunities to strengthen the client's overall risk management strategy.
  • Evaluate exposures involving high-value residences, multiple properties, luxury and collector vehicles, valuable articles, fine art, jewelry, watercraft, recreational vehicles, excess liability, domestic staff, trusts, LLC-owned property, and other sophisticated personal risks.
  • Review replacement cost estimates, appraisals, schedules of valuables, umbrella limits, underlying liability requirements, and other coverage considerations.
  • Educate clients regarding coverage options, exclusions, limitations, deductibles, carrier requirements, and risk mitigation strategies.
  • Coordinate with Risk Advisors on complex coverage recommendations, significant account changes, and opportunities to enhance the client's insurance program.

Renewal & Marketing

  • Lead the client service aspects of the renewal process, ensuring accounts are reviewed well in advance of expiration and that outstanding information is obtained timely.
  • Analyze renewal terms, pricing, coverage changes, carrier recommendations, and underwriting requirements.
  • Market accounts to appropriate carriers when necessary, including preparing submissions, gathering underwriting information, analyzing proposals, and comparing coverage options.
  • Prepare clear coverage comparisons and recommendations that help clients understand differences among carrier options.
  • Negotiate with carrier partners when appropriate to obtain favorable coverage terms and solutions.
  • Proactively communicate significant premium changes, coverage modifications, underwriting concerns, and available alternatives to clients.

New Business & Account Transitions

  • Partner with Risk Advisors on the onboarding and implementation of new high net worth personal lines accounts.
  • Review prospective client insurance programs to identify exposures and assist with developing appropriate coverage recommendations.
  • Obtain applications, underwriting information, appraisals, loss history, and supporting documentation required for placement.
  • Coordinate the issuance, review, and delivery of new policies and ensure coverage is accurately reflected in agency systems.

Carrier & Underwriting Relationships

  • Develop strong working relationships with high-net-worth personal lines carrier partners and underwriting teams.
  • Serve as a knowledgeable liaison between clients and carriers regarding underwriting requirements, inspections, risk improvement recommendations, and coverage considerations.
  • Coordinate property inspections, valuations, appraisal requirements, and underwriting follow-up.
  • Stay informed about carrier appetite, products, underwriting guidelines, coverage enhancements, and changes affecting the affluent personal insurance marketplace.

Ongoing Service & Administration

  • Process and/or oversee endorsements, cancellations, evidence of insurance, mortgagee and lienholder requests, automobile changes, valuable-article schedules, and other account transactions.
  • Review policies, endorsements, binders, and other documents for accuracy.
  • Maintain complete, accurate, and timely documentation of client communications and account activity in Applied EPIC.
  • Coordinate with claims personnel and carrier representatives to support clients through the claims process while maintaining appropriate agency and carrier roles.
  • Identify potential cross-selling opportunities or newly emerging exposures and partner with the Risk Advisor as appropriate.
  • Provide backup and support to Personal Lines team members when needed.
  • Stay current on personal insurance trends, emerging risks, carrier developments, and industry best practices through professional development and training.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
Minimum Education/Abilities/Skills
  • Active Property & Casualty insurance license required.
  • High school diploma or GED required; associate or bachelor's degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of personal lines insurance experience, preferably including direct responsibility for affluent or high net worth personal insurance accounts.
  • Strong technical knowledge of personal insurance coverages, forms, underwriting practices, and risk management concepts.
  • Experience managing complex accounts involving multiple properties, high-value homes, valuable articles, excess liability, luxury automobiles, and other specialized exposures.
  • Strong Microsoft Office skills.
Additional Qualifications
  • Experience with Applied EPIC and Fulcrum desired but not required
  • Desire to pursue Professional Designations e.g. CISR, CPRM, CPRIA

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation

  • The base salary range for this position is $60,000 to $73,000 annually. Individual compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors including relevant experience, skills, education, and internal equity.
  • Additional Compensation: This position is eligible for an annual discretionary bonus and incentive compensation.

Benefits

Eligible employees are offered a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Employer-provided life and disability insurance
  • Paid time off, paid holidays
  • Applicable paid and unpaid leaves
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan

Account Manager, Beneficial Electrification

Location: Poughkeepsie, NY (remote with local travel)


Ready to make a difference?


ICF is seeking an Account Manager to support our clients and projects in our electric vehicle (EV) and Beneficial Electrification programs in the Central New York area. The Account Manager will provide program recruitment and technical support services for customers considering electrifying their light-, medium-, and heavy-duty fleet vehicles. 


This position will be home-based and will require local travel to visit electric vehicle charging sites and meet with commercial customers in the New York area. The Account Manager will be responsible for working with end-users and dealers to explain the benefits of fleet electrification, working with fleet modeling tools to calculate financial and emission savings potential of conversions, presenting and discussing savings analysis, and supporting customers to move projects forward in various ways. 


ICF’s Beneficial Electrification and EV programs support customers in their switch from fossil fuel to electric equipment.  From light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles to buildings and industrial equipment, stakeholders are evaluating their options to electrify and reduce emissions. ICF helps utilities and companies evaluate these opportunities and support delivering those financial and decarbonization benefits. 


Why you will love working here: 

  • Quality of life: Flexible workplace arrangements, work-life balance 
  • Investment of the community: Donation matching, volunteer opportunities 
  • Investment in you: Tuition reimbursement, access to professional development resources, 401k matching, Employee Stock Purchase Plan 
  • And many, many more (Ask your recruiter for more details!) 

What you will be doing: 

  • Conduct calls and in-person meetings with commercial, industrial, and public fleet customers daily. 
  • Educate customers on the benefits of fleet electrification and related technologies. 
  • Calculate financial savings potential of conversion opportunities. 
  • Log outreach and meeting activities in program CRM tool. 
  • Discuss fleet electrification with customers to identify barriers to electrification for each participating customer and identify support services to overcome those barriers. 
  • Provide financial and business case analysis for deployment options that best fit the customer’s need (buy, lease, energy as a service). 
  • Act as a liaison between the utility distribution group and customer to evaluate new load and coordinate transformer upgrades, if required. 
  • Support customer upgrade evaluation for customer side upgrade needs. 
  • Internal and external (budgeting, procurement, board meetings) stakeholder support to answer questions with constituent groups. 
  • Assist customer in identifying and submitting for available grant and funding opportunities that can support vehicle or infrastructure deployments. 
  • Deliver technical training content and/or live training sessions to help customers familiarize staff with EVs and EV charging infrastructure, maintenance, and other aspects of fleet conversions. 
  • Lead or support project research to support customer’s deployment needs with codes, zoning, parking, building or other project viability requirements. 
  • Support customer in acquiring vendor bids for site development, vehicles and equipment, or other services as needed. 
  • Attend client sponsored and industry events to engage customers and trade allies 
  • Ensure high customer satisfaction with the program. 
  • Must have a reliable vehicle for local travel. Requirements are between 20% to 30% of the time. (reimbursement for mileage provided)

OR

  • 4+ years experience in Account Management, Sales, Customer Engagement, Energy Efficiency and/or Consulting or a related area.

AND


  • Must be able to pass a background check, have a valid driver’s license, and successfully pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check and drug screening.

  • Technical experience with light, medium, and/or heavy-duty electric vehicles and/or electric vehicle charging equipment 
  • Experience working with a Utility either directly or in a consultative capacity
  • Familiarity with a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) application such as Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics 
  • Data Analysis experience utilizing Tableau or PowerBi

  • Computer experience, with strong proficiency in MS Office Applications (Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Excel)
  • Excellent written communication and presentation skills

jobs.description:
Provectus is an AI consultancy founded in 2010 and led by its founders. As an AWS Premier Partner and an Anthropic Preferred Partner, we help Financial Services & Insurance and Healthcare & Life Sciences companies design, build, and operate production AI systems. With offices across North America, LATAM, and EMEA, we work with clients worldwide.

We are hiring an Account Executive to turn incoming enterprise leads into signed consulting engagements. Clients buy multi-month consulting engagements. You won't build pipeline from scratch. Anthropic and AWS share qualified enterprise leads with us.

Your job has four parts:

  • Qualify those leads quickly.

  • Run discovery with buyers at banks, insurers and life sciences companies.

  • Scope the work with our architects.

  • Close.

What you'll do:

    • Pick up new leads as they arrive, decide which to pursue, and be able to explain why.
    • Run discovery calls with business and technology leaders. Map their process, data, regulatory constraints, budget and decision path.
    • Work with delivery leads and architects to scope proposals and SOWs that we can deliver. You are selling consulting engagements, not software licenses.
    • Negotiate and close to a signed SOW, with the Chief Commercial Officer joining larger deals.
    • Run the full sales cycle: discovery, solution scoping, proposal, negotiation, close.
    • Translate Anthropic's product roadmap and partnership incentives into the client propositions.
    • Keep Anthropic and AWS partner reps informed on the leads they share, and take part in joint pipeline reviews.
    • Keep the CRM current and forecast your deals accurately.
    • Bring buyer objections and patterns from each industry back to leadership and marketing.
    • Travel for client meetings, up to 30% of your time.

What You Need:

  • 2–4 years in a client-facing commercial role in a consulting or IT services firm where you closed deals yourself, such as account executive, account manager, or consultant who owned client sales. Be ready to share the specifics: what you closed, at what size, and how long each deal took.

  • OR experience with banks, insurers, or pharma/biotech companies in one of these roles: selling services or technology to them (including smaller deals you closed yourself or larger deals where you supported the lead); working on client projects at a consulting firm, including proposals or scoping; or working inside one of these companies on projects where you helped evaluate and select outside vendors.

  • Working knowledge of Financial Services (banking, insurance, capital markets) or Life Sciences (pharma, biotech). You have worked in the industry or sold into it, and you can discuss a buyer's process and regulatory constraints in their terms.

  • Experience selling services engagements or complex B2B deals with several stakeholders.

  • Clear written and spoken communication with director-, VP- and C-level buyers.

  • Comfort handling a steady volume of leads and choosing where to spend your time.

Strong plus:

  • Experience selling AI/ML, data or cloud services.

  • Experience working partner-referred leads from Anthropic, AWS, GCP or Azure.

Why this role is worth your time:

  • Leads arrive every day, so your time goes into closing rather than prospecting.

  • You learn enterprise AI consulting sales in two regulated industries.

  • You close with support: our architects scope the work with you, and the Chief Commercial Officer joins larger negotiations.

  • The delivery team can execute what you sell: 350+ people, 150+ certified architects, and 100+ customers in production.

  • Work at the intersection of two AI partnerships: Anthropic and AWS.

  • High-impact role with direct visibility to leadership.

Compensation and benefits:

    • Base $90–120K + commission, OTE range $140–170K. The salary range is determined through interviews and a review of the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant, and alignment with market data.

    • B2B contract model or full-time model.

    • Unlimited vacation policy.

    • Generous health, vision, and dental insurance, and life insurance.

    • 401(k) matching plan.

Our process:

    1. A 30/45-minute call with our recruiter.

    2. An interview with the AE about a deal you closed.

    3. An interview with the Chief Commercial Officer.

    4. An interview with the CEO.

jobs.title: HRIS, Benefits & Leave Lead
jobs.excerpt: Accompany Health is on a mission to give patients with complex needs the dignified, high-quality care they deserve but rarely receive.
jobs.description:
Accompany Health is on a mission to give patients with complex needs the dignified, high-quality care they deserve but rarely receive. A primary, behavioral, and social care provider, Accompany Health walks alongside patients for their entire care journey, offering at-home and virtual care, as well as 24/7 support. Partnering with innovative payors, Accompany Health is powered by remarkable care teams, elegant technology, and a commitment to evidence-based practice.

We build long-term relationships with our patients so they know, without question, that our team is here for them day or night, year after year. We focus on the health outcomes most important to our patients to make it clear that they lead the way.

To achieve our mission, we collaborate with community-based organizations, local providers, and health plans. Led by our empathetic care teams, guided by proven care models, and powered by our own technology, we deliver a level of service that our communities rightfully deserve but rarely receive.

While our headquarters is in Bethesda, MD, our teams are distributed across the country. If you’re eager to make a tangible difference in people’s lives, to help correct long-standing disparities in health care, join us.

About the role:

Our care teams show up for patients around the clock. This role makes sure we show up for them — that their data is right, their benefits work, and when life happens, their leave or accommodation is handled with clarity and care.

As the HRIS, Benefits & Leave Lead, you will own three connected areas of People Operations:

  • HRIS: You are our Rippling expert — the person who knows the platform inside and out, leads every configuration change and integration, and builds the reporting our leaders rely on.
  • Leave & Accommodations: You will bring leave of absence and ADA accommodation administration in-house from our current vendor, and become the trusted, employee-facing partner for every leave and accommodation request.
  • Benefits: You will run day-to-day benefits administration and lead our partnership with our benefits broker to shape plans that fit a growing, distributed workforce.

You’ll work closely with People leadership, Business Leaders, Payroll, Finance, and IT.

Responsibilities will include:

Leave of Absence & ADA Accommodations:

  • Lead the transition of leave and accommodation administration from our external vendor to an in-house program, including process design, employee-facing materials, templates, tracking, and a clean handoff of open cases
  • Serve as the primary, employee-facing point of contact for all leave requests — medical, parental, family care, military, and state-mandated leaves — guiding employees from first notice through return to work
  • Manage the ADA interactive process end to end: intake, medical documentation, partnering with managers to identify effective accommodations, and documenting the dialogue and outcome. Escalate complex cases to People leadership and legal counsel
  • Determine eligibility and track entitlements under FMLA, the ADA, and applicable state and local leave and paid family and medical leave programs across a multistate workforce
  • Partner with Payroll and Finance to ensure pay during leave is accurate and confirmed — including PTO usage, salary continuation, disability and state benefit coordination, benefit premium deductions while on leave, and reinstatement at return to work
  • Coordinate with disability carriers and state agencies on claim status and required filings
  • Maintain medical and accommodation records confidentially and separately from personnel files
  • Track leave and accommodation trends, and recommend policy and process improvements

Benefits Administration & Strategy:

  • Own day-to-day benefits administration: new hire enrollment, qualifying life events, terminations, COBRA, and carrier data feeds
  • Serve as the first point of contact for employee benefits questions — triage, resolve, and escalate to the broker or carriers when needed, with fast and empathetic follow-through
  • Lead the working relationship with our benefits broker: bring utilization, cost, and employee feedback data to renewal discussions, evaluate plan design options, and present recommendations to People leadership and Finance
  • Run annual open enrollment end to end: plan setup in Rippling, employee communications and education, and post-enrollment audit
  • Reconcile monthly benefits invoices against enrollment data and resolve discrepancies with carriers and the broker
  • Ensure compliance with ACA (including 1094-C/1095-C reporting), COBRA, ERISA, HIPAA privacy, Section 125, and required employee notices, in partnership with our broker and counsel

HRIS & People Data (Rippling):

  • Serve as Accompany’s Rippling owner and subject-matter expert across all modules in use: configuration, custom fields, policies, workflows, approval chains, and user permissions
  • Own intake, prioritization, and delivery of all HRIS change requests, assessing downstream impact on payroll, benefits, and reporting before anything goes live.
  • Lead integrations between Rippling and connected tools (e.g., Greenhouse, benefits carriers, payroll, finance, and IT/identity systems): scope requirements, coordinate with vendors, test, and monitor data feeds over time
  • Design and build sophisticated reports and dashboards — headcount, turnover, compensation, leave, benefits cost and utilization, and compliance reporting (e.g., EEO-1, ACA) — and translate the data into clear insights for People leadership, Finance, and executives
  • Protect data integrity through regular audits, documented controls, and role-based access based on least privilege, with particular care for sensitive and medical information
  • Evaluate new Rippling functionality and automation opportunities; recommend and lead rollouts and upgrades
  • Document configurations, integrations, and processes so our systems scale and knowledge never lives in one person’s head
  • Train and support employees and People team members on self-service functionality

What makes you a fit for the team:

  • You take ownership of accuracy. Data, pay, and compliance details matter to you because you know they matter to people
  • You’re a builder. You’ve stood up processes from scratch and you like making them better
  • You meet people well in hard moments. Employees come to you during illness, new parenthood, and family crises; you respond with warmth, clarity, and discretion
  • You translate complexity. You can explain a system change to IT, a leave entitlement to an employee, and a cost trend to Finance
  • You’re comfortable in a fast-paced, evolving environment and can prioritize across competing demands
  • You’re motivated by supporting a mission-driven organization scaling to serve more patients and communities

What success looks like:

  • First 90 days: You own the Rippling change queue, have completed an audit of core data and permissions, mapped every integration, and inventoried open leave cases with our current vendor
  • First 6 months: Leave and ADA administration is running in-house with documented processes, templates, and a working pay-confirmation rhythm with Finance and Payroll
  • First 12 months: You have led a full benefits renewal and open enrollment with data-backed recommendations, and a reporting suite is live for People leadership and Finance

Desired skills and experience

  • Required
    • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience
    • 5+ years of experience across HRIS, benefits, and leave administration, with hands-on depth in at least two of the three
    • 3+ years as a primary administrator of a modern HRIS, including configuration, workflows, permissions, and building complex reports
    • Direct experience administering FMLA, managing the ADA interactive process, and handling state leave programs, ideally across multiple states
    • Experience administering benefits and working directly with brokers and carriers, including open enrollment and invoice reconciliation
    • Advanced analytical and data skills in Excel/Google Sheets (e.g., pivot tables, lookups, reconciliations)
    • Working knowledge of ACA, COBRA, ERISA, and HIPAA requirements
    • Excellent judgment, discretion, and communication with both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Preferred
    • Expert-level Rippling administration, including custom workflows, custom fields, and report building
    • Experience with Rippling, Greenhouse, and Google Workspace
    • Experience building or managing system integrations (payroll, benefits, ATS) and working knowledge of APIs, data feeds, or automation tools
    • Experience bringing leave administration in-house or transitioning between leave vendors
    • Relevant certifications such as CLMS (Certified Leave Management Specialist), CEBS, SHRM-CP/SCP, or PHR/SPHR
    • Experience supporting a clinical or 24/7 workforce, or a background in healthcare, health tech, or a high-growth startup

Salary ranges are based on role, level, and location, and reflect the minimum to maximum target for new hire pay in each position. Depending on the role, you may also be eligible for bonus, equity, and benefits. Where you fall within the range depends on factors such as your location, skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Our talent team is happy to share more details on the specific range for your location during the hiring process.

Pay Transparency
$135,000—$155,000 USD

Our people are the foundation of our success. By joining our growing team at Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI), a subsidiary of McKesson, you will have the opportunity to become part of one of the largest community-based cancer programs to advance oncology treatments and improve outcomes for cancer patients across the globe. People who live with cancer – those who work to prevent it, fight it, and survive it – are at the heart of every decision we make. Bringing the most innovative medical minds together with the most passionate caregivers in their communities, we are transforming care and personalizing treatment. Through clinical excellence and cutting-edge research, SCRI is redefining cancer care around the world.

Our Senior Payment Reimbursement Analyst is responsible for overseeing and optimizing the end-to-end process of vendor invoice review, reconciliation, and payment within the Revenue Cycle department. This role ensures the highest standards of accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with contractual and regulatory requirements. The Senior Analyst acts as a key liaison between vendors, internal departments, and sponsors, resolving complex billing discrepancies, supporting reimbursement workflows, and driving financial integrity across the vendor payment lifecycle. This position is expected to lead process improvements, mentor junior staff, and contribute to strategic initiatives.


This is a remote position based in the US; relocation assistance and visa sponsorship are not available.


Duties include and are not limited to:

  • Lead the contracting and payment processes for all vendors utilized by managed sites, ensuring compliance and efficiency.
  • Review, reconcile, and approve complex vendor invoices (including those with medical terminology, drug names, and CPT codes) for timely and accurate payment.
  • Oversee the transition of high-volume vendors to data file submissions and establish optimal payment cadences.
  • Promptly review all HCFA/UB vendor claim forms for payment and work with high volume vendors to transition to a data file submission and an appropriate cadence
  • Analyze and interpret vendor contracts and coverage analysis documents, providing guidance on research vs. standard of care reimbursement.
  • Serve as the escalation point for complex billing issues, collaborating with vendors, sponsors, and internal stakeholders to resolve discrepancies.
  • Advance processed SCRI vendor data to the Data Integrity team for prompt reimbursement from sponsors
  • Advance processed vendor data, completed check request, and support to the AP team for vendor reimbursement
  • Maintain and enhance business relationships with departments, sites, vendors, and sponsors/CROs, including leading meetings and negotiations.
  • Promptly review and accurately resolve patient concerns as they arise through direct vendor to patient billing

Qualifications include:

  • Bachelor's Degree required, Master's Degree preferred.

  • Advanced research and analytical techniques for financial data evaluation.

SCRI’s research network brings together more than 1,300 physicians who are enrolling patients into clinical trials at more than 200 locations in 20+ states across the U.S. Please click here to learn more about our research offerings.

WHY JOIN US

■ Design what a modern, AI-first SEO and web delivery team looks like, not just run the old one.

■ Work with the latest AI tools, with leadership that backs you to use them.

■ Real ownership: a team, a product and a direct line to the Head of Product.

■ A Brisbane agency big enough to matter and small enough to move fast.

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

We're turning SEO and websites from custom, one-off work into standard products that deliver the same quality for every client, every month. A Brisbane agency serving a large portfolio of Australian small and medium businesses. Our delivery team already uses AI every day: Claude, custom skills and automated workflows for research, content and tickets. We don't grow by adding headcount every time we add clients. We grow by building smarter systems. You'll own that system for SEO and web delivery, and work with our Head of Product to make it standard, measurable and scalable.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

1. Own SEO and web delivery, end to end

■ Make sure every SEO and website deliverable is planned, assigned, checked and shipped on time. ■ Keep a live view of workload, deadlines and risks, so nothing sits waiting and nothing surprises a client.

■ Be the escalation point when delivery goes off track, and fix the cause, not just the ticket.

2. Standardise our SEO and web products

■ Define exactly what each SEO and website package includes, and how it gets delivered.

■ Turn that into playbooks, SOPs, templates and QA checklists the whole team follows.

■ Work with the Head of Product and teams across the business (sales, account management, marketing) to design and launch new SEO and web packages.

3. Lead and grow the delivery team

■ Manage our distributed SEO, content and web team day to day.

■ Set clear goals, KPIs and a weekly operating rhythm: stand-ups, 1:1s, reviews.

■ Coach people to solve problems themselves, and help hire as the team grows.

■ Find the manual, repetitive steps in research, audits, content, QA and reporting, and redesign them with AI.

■ Build and share Claude skills, prompts and automations (n8n or similar) the team uses daily.

■ Set guardrails so AI output is accurate, on-brand and safe with client data.

■ Measure the result: hours saved, faster turnaround, fewer errors.

■ Team leadership. 2+ years managing a delivery team, including remote or distributed staff across time zones.

jobs.excerpt: About Positron AIPositron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference.
jobs.description:
About Positron AI

Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference. Our first-generation ASIC, Asimov, is a cutting-edge accelerator targeting frontier AI workloads, with additional generations already underway.

Role Overview

This engineer will improve end-to-end large language model (LLM) inference performance on Positron's custom AI accelerators, including our FPGA-based Atlas systems and our Titan systems built on the Asimov ASIC. The work spans hardware-accelerated attention, accelerator tuning, distributed KV cache, and scalable inference serving architectures. It covers profiling, algorithms, GPU-side data preparation, host-to-device data movement, runtime behavior, and measurement on production-relevant models.

You will join a small, performance-focused team that is expected to optimize the whole stack, and not merely tune isolated kernel interfaces. The goal is to sustain a repeatable path from observing workload symptoms to identifying root causes and creating measured improvements.

Key Responsibilities

Performance Profiling and Optimization

  • Profile and optimize latency, throughput, utilization, and efficiency across hardware-accelerated attention, accelerator configuration, the device runtime, host software, and on-device execution.
  • Use performance counters, hardware and software traces, telemetry, and simulation to isolate regressions and validate fixes.

Distributed Inference and KV Cache

  • Develop and optimize distributed inference capabilities, including efficient KV cache management and data movement across heterogeneous hardware.

Benchmarking and Test Infrastructure

  • Build representative benchmarks and workload traces that expose bottlenecks in compute, memory, chip-to-chip interconnect, networking, scheduling, and model loading.
  • Partner with test engineers embedded in the team to turn performance findings into durable regression tests and release gates.

Architecture Influence

  • Influence hardware and software architecture and interfaces where measured performance reveals a structural limitation.

Required Qualifications

  • Strong C++ and Python skills, with hands-on experience profiling and optimizing complex systems that exercise Linux VFIO interfaces..
  • Deep understanding of memory hierarchy, concurrency, data movement, batching, scheduling, and performance measurement.
  • Hands-on experience using profilers, counters, traces, and statistical methods to distinguish signal from noise.
  • Demonstrated ability to debug across application, runtime, driver, firmware, and hardware boundaries.
  • Experience bringing up software on new silicon, and debugging and analyzing performance optimizations in customer production deployments.
  • Enthusiasm for AI-accelerated software development, including using coding agents and orchestrating subagents to move faster without compromising engineering outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with CUDA, HIP, Triton, GPU kernel development, distributed inference, or KV cache systems.
  • Familiarity with transformer inference, mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, model serving, FPGA or ASIC accelerators.
  • Working knowledge of Perfetto, Linux perf, eBPF, simulation, or hardware performance counters.

Leveling & Scope

While this role is currently posted at a specific level, we are a growth-oriented organization and are open to hiring at a more senior level for the right candidate. Please note that this job description serves as a focused but generalized overview of the role; specific responsibilities and impact expectations will be tailored to the experience and seniority of the final hire.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12 months:

  • A baseline performance scorecard exists for priority workloads, with repeatable measurement and clearly identified bottlenecks.
  • At least one major bottleneck in hardware-accelerated attention, accelerator tuning, or distributed inference has been removed, with an automated regression guard in place.
  • A key distributed inference data path has a working implementation with quantified end-to-end cost.

Why Join Us?

  • Work on a small, high-leverage performance team with the mandate to debug and improve the full stack, from application code down to firmware and hardware, rather than being confined to a single layer.
  • Help shape the distributed inference architecture and KV cache strategy for a custom inference accelerator at a formative stage, with direct influence over interfaces and system design.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role is $200,000 – $300,000.

Please note that the figures provided represent the base salary range only and do not include other elements of our total compensation package, equity, or comprehensive benefits.

At Positron AI, we value the unique expertise each candidate brings. While the range above reflects our typical expectation for the position, we reserve the flexibility to exceed this range for candidates whose specialized skills, significant experience, or unique qualifications fall outside the standard scope of the role. Final offers are determined based on a variety of factors, including internal equity, and individual impact.

Benefits & Perks

We want you to do your best work and feel confident that you and your family are taken care of. That means comprehensive coverage, real time to rest, and support for your future.

Health and wellness

  • Fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your dependents.
  • Company-paid life and disability coverage, with voluntary options to add more.
  • Supplemental hospital, critical illness, and accident coverage available.

Time off and flexibility

  • 13 paid company holidays.
  • Remote-first culture with a company-provided computer and home office setup.

Compensation and future

  • Competitive salary and equity.
  • 401(k) with company matching, eligible from day one.

Visa Support

This position is open to candidates currently authorized to work in the U.S. We cannot provide new visa sponsorship for this role but are open to facilitating H-1B visa transfers for eligible candidates.

Our data flows from our applications, product events and business systems, in a highly regulated healthcare context. This role exists to build the platform that makes sure that data arrives complete, on time and safe to use, so Product, leadership, RevOps and Finance work from the same numbers.

You will be the first data engineer in a new data team that sits in Product, works across the company and reports to the Head of Data. You will own the platform that moves our data into Snowflake and shape the architecture decisions around it: which tools we build on, how pipelines are orchestrated and monitored, and how data infrastructure is managed as code.

What to expect

This is what you can expect from us as a Senior Data Engineer:

  • Purposeful work – your work gives the teams serving hospitals and aftercare providers data they can trust.

  • Real ownership – as the first data engineer in a new team, you shape the data platform and its tooling.

  • Company culture – we believe in flat hierarchies that promote high performance and strong team dynamics. We foster an environment characterized by mutual respect, loyalty, and recognition. Together, we strive for our goals – and expect the same from you.

  • Flexibility – want to pick up your child from daycare? Like to exercise during lunch? We'll support you. We are a remote-friendly company offering flexible working hours. Workations are also possible by arrangement.

  • Edenred card – which you can use according to your needs.

Extra vacation day – so you can celebrate your birthday with your loved ones, you'll have the day off.

This is how you will make an impact as a Senior Data Engineer:

  • Data from our application databases, product events and SaaS tools needs to reach Snowflake reliably. You build and run that ingestion and decide where to buy a managed connector and where to build.

  • Our pipelines need clear dependencies, retries, alerting and SLAs. You set up orchestration so a failed or partial load stops downstream work instead of silently producing wrong numbers.

  • New products need event pipelines. You design them together with engineers, keeping patient data out of analytics events by design.

  • Product and Finance need to work from the same definitions. You maintain the dbt models that connect product usage with customer, billing and revenue data.

  • Our CRM (HubSpot) and our internal systems need to talk to each other. You build the data flows between them, including two-way synchronisation where it is needed.

  • Data quality problems need to be caught before a dashboard or a board report does. You establish validation, monitoring and alerting.

  • Our data needs strong privacy and access controls. You enforce role-based access and masking in Snowflake, pseudonymisation, and deletion that propagates across raw and modelled data.

  • Data code needs the same engineering standards as our product code. You bring code review, testing, documentation and CI/CD to it.

How we build

We run a modern cloud-native stack to move, model and protect data reliably in a regulated healthcare environment.

  • Cloud: AWS (The European Sovereign Cloud partition)

  • Runtime: Kubernetes (EKS) and Postgres (RDS)

  • Warehouse and modelling: Snowflake (EU), dbt

  • Orchestration: Airflow or Dagster (being introduced)

  • BI: Looker

  • Observability: Datadog

  • CI/CD: GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Actions

  • Infrastructure: CloudFormation

  • Business systems: HubSpot, Chargebee

Requirements

  • Several years (typically 5 or more) building production data pipelines, as a data engineer or as a backend engineer on data-intensive systems.

  • Strong Python: you write tested, maintainable production code, not only scripts.

  • Advanced SQL, including window functions, CTEs and query optimisation.

  • Production experience with Snowflake or a comparable cloud warehouse: compute sizing and cost control, role-based access, masking, and performance tuning.

  • Experience with dbt, or a similar tool for tested and documented transformations.

  • Solid ingestion fundamentals: initial versus incremental loads, change data capture from Postgres, idempotency, schema evolution, late and out-of-order data, and backfills.

  • Production experience with an orchestrator such as Airflow or Dagster.

  • Experience with AWS and with deploying your own work in containers.

  • A data quality mindset: you profile data, test assumptions and build checks.

  • Practical knowledge of GDPR: you can identify personal data and implement pseudonymisation, access control and deletion.

  • You use AI coding tools in your daily work and know where they help and where they need checking.

  • Ability to own decisions as the only data engineer and to explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers.

  • Preference for writing over talking, resulting in clear, concise, yet complete documentation and asynchronous communications.

  • Fluent English, written and spoken. Other languages are a plus.

Bonus points

  • Healthcare or regulated-domain experience (e.g. ISO 27001, C5).

  • Integrating CRM and SaaS systems such as HubSpot or Salesforce, including reverse ETL or two-way sync.

  • Designing product event tracking (e.g. Snowplow or Segment).

  • Kubernetes in production.

  • Reading and changing Go code.

  • Managing Snowflake as code.

  • German language skills.

Our values

This will help you decide if you want to join us – our values are:

  • Strong opinions, weakly held. We adapt, negotiate trade-offs, and reconsider decisions when necessary. We don't stick to one implementation – we re-evaluate and adjust as needed (including throwing away the old one).

  • Pragmatic choice of tools and avoidance of one-size-fits-all thinking.

  • Bringing professionalism and empathy to how you work with others.

  • Strong belief in solid technical fundamentals and preference for understanding and first principles over memorization.
