jobs.excerpt: At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
jobs.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

About the Brand & Communications TeamThe Brand & Communications team crafts and shares Affirm’s story to build trust, elevate our brand, and drive business impact. The Brand Creative team leads conceptually bold, strategically grounded work across channels—from owned content to paid media. The PR & Communications team handles internal and external messaging, ensuring our values show up in media, exec visibility, and employee storytelling. Together, we manage brand strategy, content, campaigns, media relations, and communications. We connect meaningfully with customers, partners, and the public while championing Affirm’s mission.

About the Role

We want more people to understand what makes Affirm different and choose us with confidence. To make that happen, we need a rigorous understanding of our audiences and a clear, measurable view of whether our story is resonating.

The Senior Manager, Narrative Intelligence will build the analytical intelligence function behind Affirm’s Brand & Communications strategy. You’ll connect original research, Affirm’s first-party data, brand and media measurement, behavioral signals, and external datasets to understand our audiences, identify what shapes their perceptions, and find where our story can connect more meaningfully.

You’ll turn a complex mix of data into a clear point of view that shapes Affirm’s narrative and the work we put into the world. Then you’ll close the loop: defining how we measure narrative performance, determining what is and isn’t working, and identifying what we should do differently as a result.

The ambition is to make intelligence an operating system for the work—not a report that arrives after it—and set a new standard for how Brand & Communications uses data to make decisions

What You’ll Do

  • Build an evidence-based understanding of our priority audiences. Lead research and analysis into who they are, what they value, how they behave, what they believe about Affirm and the category, and what could change those beliefs. Use segmentation, surveys, behavioral data, and other analytical approaches to identify the variables that matter most.
  • Develop Affirm’s narrative measurement framework. Define the metrics, methodologies, and baselines we use to evaluate narrative performance across audiences, channels, and time horizons. Partner with Analytics, User Research, Marketing, and other teams to strengthen attribution, experimentation, and our understanding of how narrative and reputation contribute to business outcomes.
  • Build the team’s intelligence system. Create the tools, dashboards, analytical standards, and shared knowledge base that make audience intelligence and performance data easy to find, interpret, and apply. Help the broader team become more analytically confident over time.
  • Own the narrative feedback loop. Build a continuous, data-informed picture of how Affirm’s story is landing. Diagnose what is breaking through, what is being misunderstood or ignored, where perceptions are shifting, and what the evidence suggests we should do next.
  • Connect the evidence. Bring together qualitative research, surveys, brand health, media and social intelligence, search and cultural signals, campaign performance, behavioral data, and Affirm’s own customer and business data. Draw on credible external research about culture, commerce, credit, and the forces shaping how people think and behave. Find patterns, test relationships, surface contradictions, and assess the strength of the evidence.
  • Turn analysis into narrative strategy. Translate findings into clear implications for Affirm’s positioning, messaging, campaigns, content, and communications planning. Partner with the Head of Story to build and evolve Affirm’s narrative based on what the data tells us.
  • Design studies that answer consequential questions. Turn ambiguous business and communications questions into testable hypotheses and rigorous research. Choose the right mix of surveys, experiments, observational analysis, and qualitative inquiry to produce evidence the team can act on.

What We Look For

  • You’re driven to understand people through data. You’re curious about the beliefs and motivations beneath human behavior and equally interested in whether the evidence supports the story being told.
  • You’ve spent 12+ years in consumer analytics, audience insights, data science, measurement, strategic intelligence, quantitative research, or a related field. You’ve used analysis to shape brand, communications, marketing, product, or creative strategy.
  • You’re highly fluent in quantitative research and analysis. You’re comfortable with survey design, segmentation, statistical inference, experimentation, measurement design, and large or imperfect datasets. You work directly with data, using tools such as SQL, statistical platforms, data visualization, or business intelligence tools.
  • You know how to build a complete picture from different forms of evidence. You can integrate qualitative insight and quantitative analysis, account for the limits of each source, and translate concepts such as trust, relevance, reputation, and narrative resonance into thoughtful analytical frameworks.
  • You turn analysis into decisions. You can take a messy body of evidence, determine which signals matter, and explain what they mean for the narrative, the work, and the choices in front of us. Your conclusions are clear, memorable, and useful to both analytical and creative audiences.
  • You work well across analytical, strategic, and creative disciplines. You can collaborate credibly with data scientists and researchers, then translate the work for writers, strategists, executives, and communications leaders.
  • You’d rather discover something inconvenient than confirm what everyone already believes. You test assumptions, challenge weak evidence, and follow the data—even when it complicates the current story.

Equity Grade - 6

Our purpose-driven approach offers an inspirational career opportunity where you can contribute to improving health outcomes for millions of patients nationwide.

Location: Remote within the United States

Job Summary
The Senior Staff Engineer on the Ops Portal team is a technical anchor at the intersection of field operations and software engineering. You will serve as the Engineering Lead within the product trio, owning the technical direction and architecture of the tools that Field, DS, and Client Operations rely on every day: Ops Portal, the Device Configurator Application (DCA), and Unified Device Diagnostics (UDD), an AI agent platform that collects device data and diagnoses issues across the fleet. 

This is a hands-on role with broad scope. It spans three products and the shared Android device platform, which is why it sits at Senior Staff. You will write production code, sign off on the team’s highest-risk changes, and shape what gets built alongside the Product Lead and Design Lead. You will also bring Android, IoT, and AI agent expertise to PatientPoint’s Engineering Architecture Group. 

What You Will Do

  • Own technical direction for Ops Portal, DCA, and UDD: architecture, standards, and release cadence. 
  • Stay hands-on. Write production code in Kotlin, Python, and Node.js, and review work across the React front end, the serverless backend, and the Android and iOS apps. 
  • Partner with the Product Lead and Design Lead from discovery through planning. Assess feasibility and surface technical constraints, capacity, and sequencing risks before commitments are made. 
  • Architect and build services and APIs for real-time device communication and remote command and control, on AWS IoT Core and MQTT, serverless AWS (Lambda, API Gateway, Cognito), and Terraform. 
  • Lead the evolution of UDD and the Ops AI assistant: AI agents on AWS Bedrock that use tools over MCP, with human-in-the-loop controls and evals that show they work. Move the product area from reactive troubleshooting toward eventual proactive, self-healing operations. 
  • Own change safety for the fleet. Sign off on the team’s highest-risk changes, such as bulk updates to tens of thousands of devices, device provisioning, and anything that lets AI act on a device, and make sure each has a staged rollout and a tested rollback. 
  • Hold the security bar: authentication and authorization, secrets, and keeping PHI out of logs, screenshots, and LLM output. 
  • Work with the other device teams that share the Android codebase (core libraries, the DMM agent, and fleet deployment tooling) so changes land safely for every team that ships from it. 
  • Ensure the product is instrumented and observable. Establish usage metrics, error tracking, and performance monitoring so the team makes evidence-based decisions. 
  • Engage with the Architecture Group: submit RFCs for significant architectural decisions, uphold org-wide standards, and lead R&D and proofs of concept in AI-assisted diagnostics, self-healing device workflows, and next-gen provisioning. 
  • Support story breakdowns, design sessions, and PR reviews. Mentor engineers and raise the team’s technical capability. 

What We Need

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience building and running production systems. 
  • Strong backend proficiency in Kotlin and/or Python, building reliable services and APIs. 
  • Hands-on experience with Android device fleets: Android app or system development (AOSP, APK deployment, ADB), device telemetry, remote command and control, and provisioning. 
  • Deep AWS experience, including AWS IoT Core and MQTT, serverless (Lambda, API Gateway, Cognito), and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform). 
  • Experience building AI agent systems: LLM tool use (MCP or equivalent), guardrails on what agents can do, and evals. 
  • Prior experience as a technical or engineering lead on a product team: owning architectural direction, setting standards, operating as a peer to product and design, and unblocking others without becoming a bottleneck. 
  • Proficiency with AI-assisted development tools (Cursor, Claude, Copilot) as part of your everyday workflow. 

Desired Qualifications

  • BLE-based configuration and mobile provisioning workflows, and familiarity with iOS and Swift (CoreBluetooth). 
  • React and Node.js, for contributing to and reviewing Ops Portal front-end and Lambda work. 
  • Digital signage or kiosk-mode Android fleets. 
  • Event streaming (Kafka or equivalent). 
  • Observability tooling (CloudWatch, X-Ray, OpenTelemetry) and product analytics (Mixpanel), with a habit of building instrumentation into everything you ship. 
  • Healthcare or other regulated environments, including HIPAA and PHI handling. 

What You Will Need to Succeed

  • Strong ownership mindset: you take problems from ambiguity to production and stay accountable after they ship. 
  • Sound architectural instincts, with the judgment to know when to keep things simple and when more structure is needed. 
  • Genuine curiosity about field operations. The domain is the product, and understanding how technicians work makes the engineering better. 
  • A collaborative, enabling leadership style that raises the team’s technical capability rather than creating dependency on you.

You'll swiftly respond to security alerts, investigate potential malicious activity, secure compromised accounts, and review change activity to prevent or minimize security events. By managing routine security tool adjustments and escalating complex issues, you'll ensure our defenses remain effective and responsive, safeguarding our client's assets and data.

jobs.excerpt: ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONSMexico – Co-op Partnership & Supplier Alignment• Build and maintain a strong, collaborative working relationship with the Mexican co-op leadership and their supply chain teams, functioning as CKE’s primary SCM interface into the market.
jobs.description:
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Mexico – Co-op Partnership & Supplier Alignment

  • Build and maintain a strong, collaborative working relationship with the Mexican co-op leadership and their supply chain teams, functioning as CKE’s primary SCM interface into the market.
  • Support the co-op in supplier alignment activities — including supplier performance reviews, category benchmarking, contract governance, and identification of sourcing optimization opportunities.
  • Drive alignment between co-op sourcing practices and CKE’s global supply chain standards, product specifications, and QA accreditation requirements.
  • Partner with the co-op to strengthen SCM processes and procedures within the market — including demand planning, inventory management protocols, supplier communication frameworks, and KPI reporting.
  • Monitor supply chain performance across the Mexican market and provide structured reporting and recommendations to the SCM Director on risks, gaps, and improvement priorities.
  • Support new product introductions and LTO execution in Mexico by ensuring local supply chain readiness, supplier capability, and co-op alignment ahead of launch.

Canada – Full Supply Chain Ownership

  • Own the end-to-end supply chain for Canada — operating as the accountable SCM lead with full responsibility for supply continuity, cost of goods, supplier performance, and distribution effectiveness.
  • Design, manage, and continuously optimize the distribution model for Canada, including distributor selection and performance management, logistics cost oversight, and service level adherence.
  • Lead demand forecasting and inventory planning for the Canadian market, working closely with franchisee operations and distributors to ensure accurate stock projections, minimize waste, and maintain appropriate safety stock levels.
  • Manage all supplier relationships in Canada end-to-end — from identification and qualification through to contract negotiation, ongoing account management, performance reviews, and strategic partnership development.
  • Set and execute the sourcing strategy for Canada, identifying opportunities to optimize cost, improve supply security, and develop competitive local and imported supply options across priority categories.
  • Negotiate supplier contracts and pricing agreements for the Canadian market, securing terms that deliver on cost, quality, service levels, and volume commitments.
  • Build strategic supplier partnerships in Canada that go beyond transactional management — aligning supplier growth plans, capacity development, and innovation pipelines with CKE’s Canadian business trajectory.
  • Ensure all Canadian suppliers and products maintain active QA accreditation status, partnering with the QA team to manage the qualification pipeline and address compliance issues proactively.
  • Engage franchisees in Canada as a strategic SCM partner — conducting regular business reviews, driving supply chain compliance, and providing guidance on cost management and supply continuity.

Caribbean & South America – Regional SCM Support & Development

  • Provide SCM support and guidance to franchisees across the Caribbean and South American markets, ensuring CKE supply chain standards, QA requirements, and approved product lists are maintained consistently.
  • Identify, prescreen, and develop regional suppliers across priority categories — working closely with QA to progress qualified candidates through the Approved Supplier process.
  • Conduct periodic RFPs, support contract reviews, and assist franchisees in benchmarking local suppliers versus import alternatives to drive cost efficiency without compromising quality or supply security.
  • Support new country entry activities across the region — including local supply base assessment, cost of goods development, distribution model evaluation, and franchise SCM onboarding.
  • Manage relationships with regional and global manufacturers serving the Americas, ensuring CKE’s growth strategy is visible to key suppliers and that regional operators benefit from contracted pricing and service terms.
  • Communicate fluently in Spanish with suppliers, franchisees, and co-op partners across Latin American and Caribbean markets, ensuring nothing is lost in translation at the operational and strategic level.

Supplier Strategy, Negotiation & Account Management

  • Maintain a structured account management cadence with all key suppliers across the Americas — including regular business reviews, performance scorecards, issue escalation processes, and joint planning sessions.
  • Develop multi-year sourcing strategies for priority categories within the region, balancing cost optimization, supply diversification, quality standards, and franchisee capability.
  • Lead commercial negotiations with regional and local suppliers, building agreements that protect CKE’s interests on cost, volume, service, and quality while fostering long-term partnership value.
  • Monitor commodity market trends relevant to the Americas region — including beef, chicken, produce, packaging, and key proteins — and proactively brief the SCM Director on pricing outlook and risk implications.
  • Identify supply chain cost reduction opportunities across the region and build business cases for SCM Director review, translating market intelligence into actionable COGS improvement initiatives.

Quality Assurance Partnership & Compliance

  • Serve as the primary SCM interface with the QA team for all Americas-related supplier qualification, audit coordination, and product approval activities.
  • Maintain accurate and current records of approved suppliers and products for all markets within the region, ensuring franchisees operate exclusively with QA-accredited supply.
  • Drive proactive QA compliance across the region — addressing non-compliant sourcing situations swiftly and working with franchisees and the co-op to implement corrective actions.
  • Support QA in coordinating supplier facility visits and audits within the region, prescreening candidates for operational capability and product volume viability prior to formal audit.

Performance Management & Reporting

  • Manage and maintain regional SCM KPI dashboards covering Mexico (co-op performance), Canada (full P&L visibility), and the broader Americas market portfolio.
  • Present supply chain performance reporting to franchisee leadership and the SCM Director on a regular cadence — providing analysis, commentary, and recommended actions, not just data.
  • Maintain a live and accurate regional database of approved suppliers and products, ensuring all records reflect current QA accreditation status and contract terms.
  • Coordinate with the SCM Director and CKE domestic distribution on US export activities for the region, including order management, export documentation, projected volumes, and franchisee cost communication.
  • Support Marketing and Culinary in executing LTO and new product calendars across the region, ensuring SCM readiness is confirmed well ahead of go-live dates.

POSITION QUALIFICATIONS / CORE COMPETENCIES

Experience & Education

  • Minimum 10 years of progressive supply chain experience, preferably within a QSR, FMCG, or multi-unit franchise environment.
  • Direct experience managing supply chain activities in Latin America and/or the Caribbean is strongly preferred — market knowledge, supplier landscape familiarity, and cultural fluency are critical to success in this role.
  • Proven experience in supplier sourcing, negotiation, and account management, with demonstrated ability to manage supplier relationships end-to-end.
  • Experience with distribution management, demand forecasting, and inventory planning in a multi-market environment.
  • New country entry or market launch experience is an advantage.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, or a related field required.

Language Requirements

  • Full professional fluency in both English and Spanish is required — written and spoken. This is a non-negotiable requirement given the nature of the regional portfolio.
  • Portuguese language skills are an advantage for South American market coverage.

Functional Competencies

  • Solid knowledge of food and packaging commodity markets relevant to the Americas region, including key proteins, produce, and imported food categories.
  • Strong analytical capability — advanced Excel required; exposure to ERP, procurement platforms, or BI/reporting tools preferred.
  • Proficiency in supply chain financial metrics: cost of goods, landed cost modeling, working capital, inventory management, and margin impact.
  • Understanding of import/export documentation, customs processes, and cross-border logistics within the Americas.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in both English and Spanish, with the ability to engage credibly with co-op leadership, franchisee executives, and supplier partners.

Leadership & Behavioral Competencies

  • Strategic and commercially driven — brings a business owner mindset to the region, balancing long-term strategy with strong execution and measurable business outcomes.
  • Strong relationship builder who earns trust with co-op partners, franchisees, and suppliers through consistency, follow-through, and cultural intelligence.
  • Organized and disciplined in managing a high-complexity, multi-market workload with competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Comfortable operating with autonomy and owning the function where required, while also functioning as a strategic partner to franchisees and co-op leadership — able to shift between ownership, influence, and partnership modes depending on the market context.
  • Proactive, decisive, and solutions-oriented — identifies risks and opportunities early, brings structured recommendations, and drives issues through to sustainable resolution.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Fast-paced, multicultural environment spanning multiple time zones, languages, and regulatory contexts across the Americas.
  • High degree of ownership and autonomy, particularly for the Canadian market, with close collaborative engagement in Mexico through the co-op structure.
  • Regular interaction with franchisee leadership, co-op management teams, supplier executives, and internal CKE cross-functional partners.

TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

  • International travel required, approximately 30%, including market visits across Mexico, Canada, the Caribbean, and South America, as well as supplier facility visits and franchisee business reviews.

jobs.description:
worum gehts?

ERP-Prozesse zukunftsfähig aufzustellen ist deine Leidenschaft und du willst die digitale Transformation unserer Kunden ganzheitlich begleiten? Dann werde Teil unseres Teams! Wir setzen in unserer expandierenden SAP Practice auf moderne Cloud-Architekturen, GROW with SAP, standardisierte Best Practices und Clean-Core-Paradigmen. Jetzt suchen wir dich, um dieses Thema bei uns maßgeblich mit aufzubauen, fachlich zu prägen und am Markt zu etablieren.
Als Senior Consultant Finance & Transformation (w/m/d) nimmst du eine Schlüsselrolle ein: Du begleitest Kunden auf Augenhöhe dabei, ihre Finanzprozesse aus der klassischen SAP-Landschaft in moderne S/4HANA Cloud-Lösungen zu überführen und fungierst als zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen Business-Anforderungen und IT. Dabei verbindest du betriebswirtschaftliches Prozessverständnis mit Moderationskompetenz, treibst Kundeninitiativen im Pre-Sales voran und gestaltest Best-Practice-Lösungen von morgen.

das wirst du tun

  • Themenaufbau & Pre-Sales: Du bringst deine Expertise proaktiv in Pre-Sales-Phasen und Discovery-Workshops ein und begeisterst Kunden für modernste Cloud-ERP-Ansätze im Rahmen von GROW with SAP.
  • Fit-to-Standard & Workshop-Moderation: Du bereitest Fit-to-Standard-Workshops vor, moderierst diese (u. a. entlang des SAP Process Navigators und SAP Signavio) und bewertest Prozessabweichungen methodisch (Delta-Scoping).
  • Prozessberatung & Record-to-Report: Du übersetzt betriebswirtschaftliche Anforderungen in standardnahe End-to-End-Finanzprozesse (Record-to-Report: u. a. Haupt-/Nebenbuchhaltung, Anlagenbuchhaltung, Kostenrechnung).
  • Funktionale Konfiguration: Über moderne Cloud-Werkzeuge wie SAP Central Business Configuration (CBC) richtest du die Prozesse passgenau und konsistent im S/4HANA Cloud-Standard ein.
  • Integrations- & Clean-Core-Design: Du konzipierst standardnahe Erweiterungen nach dem Clean-Core-Prinzip und stimmst Integrationsszenarien mit angrenzenden Bereichen (Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay) sowie der SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) ab.
  • Datenmigration & Testmanagement: Du berätst Kunden bei der Datenbereinigung und -migration (z. B. mit dem SAP Migration Cockpit) und nutzt moderne Plattformen wie SAP Cloud ALM für die Erstellung von Testfällen und die UAT-Begleitung.
  • Change Enablement & Hypercare: Du führst praxisnahe Key-User-Trainings durch, verankerst das Cloud-Mindset beim Kunden und sicherst eine verlässliche Go-Live- und Hypercare-Phase.

das bringst du mit

  • Mehrjährige Praxiserfahrung in SAP-Einführungs- oder Transformationsprojekten mit klarem Fokus auf Finanz- und Controllingprozesse (FI/CO). Erste Berührungspunkte mit S/4HANA Cloud (Public oder Private Edition) sind von Vorteil.

  • Ein grundlegendes Verständnis für Schnittstellen zu Logistikprozessen (z. B. Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay) und die Integrationsmöglichkeiten der SAP BTP runden dein Profil fachlich ab.
  • Idealerweise verfügst du über Zertifizierungen im SAP Cloud-Umfeld (z. B. SAP Certified Associate – S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, Financial Accounting oder SAP Activate) – falls nicht, unterstützen wir dich gerne beim Erwerb.
  • Du moderierst Workshops souverän, trittst vor Fachbereich, IT-Entscheidungsträgern sowie Management empathisch und überzeugend auf und kannst komplexe Themen verständlich vermitteln.

das hast du davon

jobs.title: Director, Government Relations — National Security and Economic Security Policy
jobs.excerpt: As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era.
jobs.description:
As the global leader in high-speed connectivity, Ciena builds the critical infrastructure powering the AI era. We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters.


The Director, Government Relations — National Security and Economic Security Policy will lead the company’s engagement on government initiatives that affect the development, manufacture, movement, sale, and trusted use of networking equipment worldwide.

Reporting to the Vice President, Government Relations, the Director will anticipate and help shape national-security, economic-security, supply-chain, cybersecurity, trade, and technology policies that may create risk or opportunity for the company. The Director will translate evolving government requirements into clear business implications and coordinate the company’s policy response across Government Relations, Legal, Trade Compliance, Product Security, Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Sales, and other functions.

The role requires a global perspective. The company is headquartered in the United States, sells to customers worldwide, manufactures primarily in Mexico and Thailand, maintains major research and development operations in India and Canada, and relies on global logistics, distribution, and component-sourcing networks. The Director must understand how national policies interact across jurisdictions and how measures directed at one country, supplier, technology, or sector can affect the company’s broader operations and market access. We are looking for a candidate in the DC area.

Core Responsibilities

Policy Monitoring and Risk Assessment

  • Working with the Vice President and other company stakeholders, develop public policy priorities for the company, weighing risk, impact, and the company’s ability to influence policy positions.
  • Monitor and assess national-security and economic-security initiatives affecting telecommunications and networking equipment, critical infrastructure, advanced technologies, global supply chains, and international trade.
  • In collaboration with company stakeholders, evaluate the direct and indirect effects of proposed policies on product design, component sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, research and development, market access, customer eligibility, and government procurement.
  • Develop practical risk assessments, scenarios, and executive recommendations that distinguish immediate compliance requirements from longer-term strategic exposure.
  • Maintain a global view of potentially conflicting or overlapping requirements across the United States and other priority markets.

Government Engagement and Advocacy

  • Working with the Vice President and other company stakeholders, develop and execute advocacy strategies for national-security policies affecting the company, including identifying priority messages, audiences, and channels for engagement.
  • Represent the company and build credible relationships with Congress, U.S. departments and agencies, foreign governments, regulators, embassies, and international institutions responsible for national security, telecommunications, cybersecurity, trade, export controls, industrial policy, procurement, and supply-chain security.
  • Develop company positions and supporting materials, including regulatory comments, consultation responses, legislative proposals, briefings, testimony, and executive talking points.
  • Advance company priorities through direct engagement, trade associations, and industry coalitions, selecting the approach best suited to each issue.

Priority Policy Portfolio

The Director’s portfolio may include:

  • Telecommunications supply-chain, product-security, and trusted-technology requirements, including vendor and country restrictions, component traceability, bills of materials, vulnerability reporting, and secure-development obligations.
  • Cybersecurity and other security conditions affecting critical-infrastructure equipment, public funding, government procurement, and telecommunications deployments.
  • Foreign investment, research-security, and cross-border technology controls affecting transactions, partnerships, R&D, and international engineering collaboration.
  • Data, cloud, artificial-intelligence, and technology-sovereignty policies affecting network architecture, market access, or customer purchasing decisions.
  • Industrial-policy incentives, manufacturing and infrastructure funding, and other government programs supporting supply-chain resilience or market growth.
  • International alignment or fragmentation among allied governments on telecommunications security and broader economic-security policy.

Leadership Attributes

The successful candidate will:

  • Think strategically while remaining attentive to operational detail.
  • Recognize the commercial consequences of policy developments before they become obvious.
  • Be comfortable operating at the intersection of national security, technology, geopolitics, and business.
  • Build trust across technical, legal, commercial, and government audiences.
  • Distinguish genuine security concerns from protectionist or discriminatory measures while engaging constructively with policymakers.
  • Exercise discretion and avoid overstating either risks or opportunities.
  • Communicate complex issues in clear language that enables timely executive decisions.
  • Combine a global outlook with an appreciation of country-specific political and regulatory dynamics.

The Must Haves:

  • Bachelor’s degree in public policy, international affairs, law, economics, political science, engineering, cybersecurity, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of government, corporate government relations, public policy, national security, international trade, telecommunications, technology, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated understanding of how national-security and economic-security policies affect globally integrated technology companies.
  • Experience engaging senior government officials, legislators, regulators, or national-security agencies.
  • Ability to analyze complex policy proposals and translate them into clear commercial and operational implications.
  • Strong writing, briefing, advocacy, coalition-building, and executive-communication skills.
  • Experience leading cross-functional work without direct authority over participating functions.
  • Sound judgment when handling sensitive, confidential, or politically complex matters.
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required.

Nice to Have:

  • Advanced degree in law, public policy, international affairs, business, cybersecurity, or a related discipline.
  • Experience with telecommunications networks, networking equipment, semiconductors, critical infrastructure, or other advanced-technology industries.
  • Familiarity with export controls, sanctions, supply-chain security, cybersecurity regulation, government procurement, domestic-content requirements, or investment screening.
  • Experience working across North America, Europe, and the Indo-Pacific.
  • Government service in a national-security, trade, economic, telecommunications, cybersecurity, or foreign-policy role.
  • Experience developing advocacy strategies that combine direct government engagement, industry coalitions, and evidence-based thought leadership.

Pay Range: The salary range for this role in the DC area is $161, 700 - $258, 300


Pay ranges at Ciena are designed to accommodate variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions, and locations, reflecting our diverse products, industries, and lines of business. Please note that the pay range information provided in this posting pertains specifically to the primary location, which is the top location listed in case multiple locations are available.

Non-Sales employees may be eligible for a discretionary incentive bonus, while Sales employees may be eligible for a sales commission. In addition to competitive compensation, Ciena offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, participation in 401(K) (USA) & DCPP (Canada) with company matching, Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP), Employee Assistance Program (EAP), company-paid holidays, paid sick leave, and vacation time. We also comply with all applicable laws regarding Paid Family Leave and other leaves of absence.

At Ciena, we are committed to building and fostering an environment in which our employees feel respected, valued, and heard. Ciena values the diversity of its workforce and respects its employees as individuals. We do not tolerate any form of discrimination.

Ciena is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status.

jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Delivery Engineer is an early-career technical role for engineers and other builders who want to develop broad expertise across technology, customer delivery, and product.
Delivery Engineers are aligned to a state or customer rather than a single product. Working alongside experienced technical and delivery leaders, they develop an end-to-end understanding of how Pearson's platforms, integrations, data flows, and operational processes work together to meet customer requirements and contractual commitments.
This is a hands-on role. Delivery Engineers demonstrate solutions, investigate technical issues, validate integrations, support implementations and production events, and work across teams to drive problems toward resolution. The role provides broad exposure to customers, products, and technology organizations and is designed to develop future leaders across Technology Readiness, Technical Product Management, Product Management, Delivery, Implementation, Support, and Technology.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop deep knowledge of assigned state or customer programs, including requirements, contractual commitments, technical solutions, integrations, configurations, and operational processes.
    • Build and maintain an end-to-end understanding of the customer solution across test administration, test delivery, scoring, reporting, data exchange, identity, infrastructure, and external integrations.
    • Translate customer, RFP, and contractual requirements into technical requirements, solution approaches, validation criteria, and delivery considerations.
    • Create and maintain system diagrams, integration flows, data flows, and other technical documentation that clearly explains how the customer solution works.
    • Develop the product and solution knowledge needed to confidently explain and demonstrate Pearson's technology capabilities to customers and internal stakeholders.
    • Participate in customer technical discussions, demonstrations, integration reviews, solution workshops, and RFP or proposal activities.
    • Provide hands-on technical support during implementation, integration testing, readiness activities, administration windows, production events, and customer escalations.
    • Investigate technical issues across systems by analyzing configurations, APIs, integrations, data flows, logs, and system behavior.
    • Partner across Engineering, Product, Quality Engineering, Implementation, Operations, Support, Security, and Infrastructure to resolve technical issues and delivery risks.
    • Support end-to-end validation to ensure systems, integrations, and operational processes collectively meet customer requirements and commitments.
    • Identify technical gaps, dependencies, risks, and product limitations, and help ensure they are understood and addressed by the appropriate teams.
    • Apply lessons from implementations, incidents, and customer feedback to improve products, documentation, processes, and future customer solutions.
    Required Qualifications
    • 1 to 3 years of experience in software engineering, systems engineering, technical support, quality engineering, or another hands-on technology discipline, or equivalent experience building, testing, integrating, or operating software systems.
    • Practical experience with software applications, APIs, integrations, data flows, cloud-based systems, or related enterprise technologies.
    • Experience troubleshooting technical issues using structured problem-solving and technical evidence.
    • Ability to read technical documentation and create or interpret system diagrams, integration flows, and data flows.
    • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to technical and nontechnical audiences.
    • Strong technical curiosity, problem-solving skills, and interest in understanding how complex systems work together.
    • Ability to collaborate across technical, product, implementation, and operational teams.
    • Interest in working directly with customers and developing confidence in customer-facing technical discussions and demonstrations.
    Preferred Qualifications
    • Experience with APIs, cloud platforms, identity and access management, logging and monitoring tools, or distributed applications.
    • Experience supporting customer implementations, integration testing, production systems, incident response, or technical escalations.
    • Experience in enterprise technology, education technology, government, or large-scale assessment.
    • Exposure to RFPs, proposals, product management, solution engineering, implementation, or delivery functions.
    What Makes Someone Successful in This Role
    Successful Delivery Engineers are curious, hands-on problem solvers who want to understand both the customer and the technology. They communicate clearly, collaborate effectively across teams, ask thoughtful questions, surface risks, and stay engaged until problems are resolved.
    They are comfortable learning beyond a single application and are motivated to understand how multiple products and integrations come together as one customer solution.
    Career Development
    The Delivery Engineer role is intentionally designed as a development path for early-career technical talent. Through direct exposure to customers, products, engineering teams, implementations, and production delivery, Delivery Engineers build the technical judgment, product understanding, and customer perspective needed for future opportunities in Technology Readiness, Technical Product Management, Product Management, Delivery, Implementation, Support, Solution Engineering, and broader Technology leadership.
    Delivery Engineers build depth on the customer and breadth across the technology ecosystem.

Compensation at Pearson is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and specific location. jobs.excerpt: What are we building? Hard Rock Digital is a fiercely focused team working to become the best online sportsbook, casino, and social gaming company in the world.
jobs.description:
What are we building?

Hard Rock Digital is a fiercely focused team working to become the best online sportsbook, casino, and social gaming company in the world. We're building a deeply curious team with a passion for learning, operating, and building new products and technologies for millions of consumers. We're customer-obsessed — we care about each customer interaction, experience, behavior, and insight, and strive to ensure we're always acting authentically.

Rooted in the kindred spirits of Hard Rock and the Seminole Tribe of Florida, Hard Rock Digital taps a brand known the world over as the leader in gaming, entertainment, and hospitality. We're taking that foundation of success and bringing it to the digital space - ready to join us?

What's the position?

Every bet and payout at Hard Rock Digital is a database transaction that has to be fast and accurate. A casino game resolves in milliseconds; settling a big sporting event moves millions of balances at once, and none can be wrong.

We're hiring Senior Database Infrastructure Engineers to own the PostgreSQL, MySQL, and ClickHouse databases behind our platform and work alongside the team that runs our CockroachDB clusters. Which engine you know best matters less than how well you understand what each one does underneath, well enough to explain why the same workload behaves differently on two of them.

A database problem rarely stays inside the database. The people who do well here follow it into the application code, the platform, and the architecture decisions, and they want their scope at Hard Rock Digital to grow with it.

Claude Code, Codex, and similar AI harnesses are part of how this team works. We use them to investigate incidents and turn one-off debugging into durable tooling, so more time goes to work that compounds: better defaults, safer migrations, and shorter incidents.

What You'll Do

Operations

  • Operate PostgreSQL and MySQL on Amazon RDS across production, staging, and development: replication, failover, backup and recovery, upgrades, and each engine's own failure modes, from autovacuum and wraparound to purge and replica lag.

  • Run ClickHouse for both operational and analytical workloads: table engines, sort keys, partitioning, merges, replication, and the ingestion paths that feed it.

  • Support CockroachDB operations, and take on more of that work as you learn the system.

Performance & Reliability

  • Trace slow queries and lock waits behind bets, settlements, and payouts to the plan, the statistics, and the schema or code that caused them.

  • Assess schema-change risk before it reaches large tables, and review schemas and queries with application teams before they ship.

  • Build observability in Prometheus, Grafana, Mimir, and Loki, join the data-layer on-call rota, and lead incident analysis and blameless postmortems.

Tooling & Influence

  • Build Python and Go tooling, and automate provisioning and recovery with Terraform.

  • Use AI harnesses daily, and verify their output against production facts before you ship it.

  • Implement and audit access controls and encryption for a regulated gaming platform.

  • Set standards that hold across engines, take part in architecture reviews, and read the source when a problem needs a code-level answer.

Requirements

What are we looking for?

  • 5+ years operating production relational databases as a DBA, Database Reliability Engineer, or Data Platform Engineer.

  • Deep production experience with PostgreSQL and MySQL, or deep experience with one and serious working experience with the other.

  • You understand these engines underneath and can compare them: PostgreSQL's heap and row versions against InnoDB's clustered index and undo log, write-ahead logging, cost-based planning, replication and what each failover option can lose, and how a columnar engine like ClickHouse differs from both.

  • Enough grounding in distributed systems (consensus, distributed transactions, consistency models) to learn CockroachDB quickly

  • Python or Go, and enough Java to debug line-of-business code.

  • Linux, infrastructure-as-code, a monitoring stack such as Grafana, AWS, and willingness to join an on-call rota.

  • Clear technical writing and speech: you can explain a hard problem to an engineer or a product manager without losing the part that matters.

How You Work

  • You learn a new system from the bottom up: the source, the design documents, and experiments you run yourself.

  • When the documentation is wrong or silent, you find out what the system really does and write it down.

  • You want a bigger job than the one you were hired into, and you look for it here.

  • You want this role to be your main professional focus, not one engagement among several.

What You've Done

  • Shipped Python or Go tooling for database operations, migration safety, or incident response that other engineers then used.

  • Investigated production incidents end-to-end, down to execution plans and source code.

  • Moved a workload between engines or across major versions, and can tell us what surprised you.

  • Took on work outside the database because the problem needed it, and changed how another team built or shipped.

  • Run ClickHouse, CockroachDB, or another distributed database in production.

  • Worked with Kafka, Materialize, or Snowflake.

  • Used AI coding agents in real work, with review habits that keep output tied to evidence.

What’s in it for you?

We offer our employees more than just competitive compensation. Our team benefits include:

  • Competitive pay and benefits

  • Flexible vacation allowance

  • A hybrid / remote working environment

  • Startup culture backed by a secure, global brand

Our vision for our business and customers is built on fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment where regardless of background or beliefs you feel able to be authentic and bring all your talent into play. We're hiring Client Experience Associates to join our team!


Your Role

  • Watch first:A Day in the Life of a Client Experience Associate

  • Answer inbound calls for our clients' businesses from home. You'll capture leads, take orders, schedule appointments, and send messages to clients.

  • Handle a range of call types, including standard answering, Active Response (where a message pops up and you are to make an outbound call to someone), live chat, relay calls, appointment setting, and legal intake calls. You'll be trained on each one.

  • Expect a steady, fast pace. Calls often come in back-to-back, and we measure performance by quality, accuracy, ready %, and after-call work time.

Your Schedule

  • 40 hours per week, mostly scheduled between 5:00 am and 8:00 pm Pacific Time.

  • A minimum of 8 hours every Friday and Saturday is required for the first 8-12 weeks after training.

  • You choose your own shifts each week, but choice is ranked by performance tier. Higher tiers pick first, so new associates should expect the least choice at the start. Flexibility is a must.

  • Attendance is tracked with a points system. Being reliable is very important!

Training

  • 2 weeks of paid training, followed by 8–12 weeks of Learning & Development, where you’ll take live calls with ongoing support.

  • During this period, you'll need full availability for 40 hours a week and can't block off holidays or vacation time.

Your Skills

  • Excellent verbal and written communication

  • A warm, upbeat tone and a genuine interest in helping people

  • A good listener who stays calm and efficient under pressure

  • Dependable: you show up for every scheduled shift, on time

  • Strong computer skills and typing at a minimum of 30 WPM

  • A growth mindset and eagerness to learn new call types and tools

Requirements

Compensation & Benefits

  • Starting at $16.00/hour

  • Benefits start after 60 days: [e.g., medical, dental, vision, EAP, PTO]

  • 401(k) with matching after one year of employment

Your System

We use a Bring Your Own Device policy. Your computer and internet connection must meet oursystem and internet requirements before you start.

About AnywhereWorks

Work is what you do, not where you do it. We’re on a mission to help the world work Anywhere. We believe people should be able to work and learn together, whether they’re communicating across a table or across the world.

We offer a diverse set of products and services to a variety of businesses, from live answering services to scheduling and payment platforms to shared working spaces. We empower people to communicate, collaborate and produce. We’re committed to building a more inclusive future of work, where people can contribute from Anywhere.

What "Anywhere" Means to Us

Other terms out in the world are “remote” “distributed” “telecommuting” – for us, these words do not speak to the experience we hope you will have working with us Anywhere.

Isolation and a lack of social interaction are common concerns when people think about Remote working. The word “Remote” itself can conjure up ideas of loneliness and being disconnected from your colleagues. That’s why we like the more empowering language of “working Anywhere”, with Anywhere representing an unconstrained, plugged-in destination.

Background Check

Please note that all candidates who receive a conditional offer of employment will be required to undergo a background check as part of the pre-employment screening process. This is to ensure the safety and integrity of our workplace and to comply with our company policies.

We comply with all requirements of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) to ensure the privacy and rights of our applicants are protected.

Equal Opportunity

AnywhereWorks is committed to providing equal opportunity employment; creating, managing, and valuing diversity in our workforce; providing a safe work environment; and fostering a culture of belonging where all employees are included, treated with dignity and respect, promoted on their merits, and placed in positions to contribute to our future success.

jobs.description:
Job Description: NDT Subject Matter Expert – Laser Shearography (Level II / Level III)

Role Type: Contractor
Location: Remote

About the Role

We are seeking experienced NDT Subject Matter Experts specializing in Laser Shearography (Level II / Level III) to contribute to an advanced aerospace inspection and AI training project. In this role, you will leverage your technical expertise to support the development and evaluation of next-generation AI systems. Your domain knowledge will help improve AI models' ability to understand, analyze, and evaluate real-world non-destructive testing (NDT) data. No prior AI experience is required.

Scope of Work

  1. Perform detailed manual analysis of laser shearography data, including fringe patterns and interferograms, to identify and characterize defects in composite materials.
  2. Review and interpret technical case studies, test logs, and inspection limits for aerospace applications in accordance with relevant NDT standards.
  3. Evaluate and document defect types, severity levels, and potential impacts on composite structures, providing detailed technical justifications.
  4. Provide comprehensive written feedback on inspection findings to support the development and improvement of technical protocols.
  5. Collaborate remotely with project managers and technical stakeholders through clear, professional written and verbal communication.
  6. Ensure all assessments and reviews are conducted without AI assistance, maintaining the highest standards of manual inspection accuracy and integrity.

Requirements

  1. Current ASNT, NAS 410, or ISO 9712 Level II or Level III certification in Laser Shearography or related NDT methods.
  2. Extensive hands-on experience with laser shearography, particularly in aerospace and advanced composite material inspection.
  3. Strong expertise in interpreting shearography fringe patterns and optical interferometry data for defect evaluation.
  4. Excellent analytical skills in defect identification, root cause analysis, and technical reporting in accordance with stringent aerospace standards.
  5. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including technical documentation and collaborative problem-solving.
  6. Good understanding of industry best practices for non-destructive inspection of composite materials.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Experience providing technical guidance or quality engineering support for NDT projects.
  2. Direct inspection, technical review, or evaluation experience in aerospace composite inspection.
  3. Familiarity with aerospace quality standards, inspection procedures, and advanced NDT methodologies.

jobs.description:
About Ellucian

Ellucian powers innovation for higher education, partnering with approximately 3,000 customers across 50 countries, serving more than 21 million students. Ellucian's AI-powered platform, trained on the richest dataset available in higher education, drives efficiency, personalized experiences, and strengthened engagement for all students, faculty and staff. Fueled by decades of experience with a singular focus on the unique needs of learning institutions, the Ellucian platform features best-in-class SaaS capabilities and delivers insights needed now and into the future. These solutions and services span the entire student lifecycle, including data-rich tools for student recruitment, enrollment, and retention to workforce analytics, fundraising, and alumni engagement. Ellucian's innovative solutions, vast ecosystem of partners and user community of more than 45,000 provides best practices leading to greater institutional success and achieving better student outcomes.


About the Opportunity

Ellucian is seeking an experienced Director, Professional Services to lead the global Data Migration & Conversion and AI & Automation capabilities within Professional Services. This role owns the strategy, operating model, people, delivery readiness, methodology, tooling, customer outcomes, and operational performance of these practices. The Director will turn proven delivery experience, regional innovation, and emerging technologies into consistent, scalable services that improve implementation speed, quality, predictability, and customer value.

The successful candidate will be equally comfortable setting a multi-year capability roadmap, leading managers and technical teams, guiding complex customer programs, and translating operations into measurable financial and delivery outcomes. This leader will partner across Professional Services, Product, Engineering, Cloud, Support, Security, Sales, Finance, Enablement, and regional teams to create a globally aligned model while preserving the strongest lessons and assets developed close to customers.

Where You Will Make an Impact
Practice Strategy and Portfolio Leadership

  • Own and communicate the global strategy, roadmap, priorities, and operating model for Data Migration & Conversion and AI & Automation within Professional Services.
  • Define a coherent portfolio of services, accelerators, reference architectures, reusable components, templates, runbooks, and implementation guidance that can be applied consistently across regions and customer engagement models.
  • Translate proven regional practices and customer delivery lessons into a scalable global methodology and tooling strategy; ensure valuable local capabilities are preserved, assessed, and incorporated into the official model where appropriate.
  • Establish clear intake, prioritization, investment, build-versus-buy, and lifecycle decisions for migration tooling, AI use cases, software automation, RPA, intelligent document processing, and related platforms.
  • Represent the practices in annual planning, executive reviews, strategic partnerships, and major cross-functional initiatives.

Data Migration and Conversion Leadership

  • Lead the teams responsible for migration discovery, source-data assessment, extraction, mapping, transformation, loading, validation, reconciliation, testing, dress rehearsals, cutover support, and post-load verification.
  • Set global standards for repeatable, controlled, and auditable migration delivery, including quality gates, data validation, test-data management, security, privacy, and customer readiness.
  • Advance the next generation of data-conversion tooling through standardized extract templates, reusable mappings, code repositories, knowledge bases, automation, and AI-assisted mapping and transformation workflows.
  • Create mechanisms to capture gold-standard conversion assets and subject-matter expertise, treat mappings and migration logic as managed intellectual property, and continuously improve them through delivery feedback.
  • Measure and improve time, cost, throughput, quality, and predictability by migration domain and customer; reduce avoidable defects and post-go-live escalations.

AI, Software Automation, and RPA Leadership

  • Lead customer-facing and internal automation capabilities spanning AI-assisted process optimization, software development, UiPath-based RPA, ServiceNow automation, intelligent document processing, APIs, and agentic or knowledge-based solutions.
  • Own the automation opportunity pipeline from process discovery and feasibility assessment through architecture, development, testing, deployment, adoption, support, and value realization.
  • Ensure solutions are secure, maintainable, well documented, reusable, and aligned with responsible-AI, data-governance, compliance, and enterprise architecture expectations.
  • Establish Agile delivery practices and portfolio visibility through Jira or equivalent tools, including a consolidated backlog, transparent priorities, delivery metrics, and clear accountability.
  • Scale an AI & Automation Center of Excellence that increases throughput, reduces dependence on scarce senior subject-matter experts, and develops sustainable global and nearshore talent.

People Care and Organizational Capability

  • Lead, coach, and develop managers, technical leads, consultants, developers, and migration practitioners; create clarity of purpose, accountability, and collaboration across a distributed global team.
  • Define organization design, role expectations, competency models, career paths, succession plans, certification priorities, and targeted enablement for data, AI, automation, software, and RPA disciplines.
  • Build a culture that moves with urgency, learns openly, shares knowledge, and builds to scale while maintaining strong engineering and consulting discipline.
  • Own workforce and capacity planning, hiring, onboarding, performance management, team health, contractor and partner strategy, and skill deployment against demand.
  • Create an environment in which early-career talent can contribute quickly while senior staff focus on architecture, governance, complex problem solving, and customer leadership.

Delivery Excellence, Operations, and Financial Performance

  • Connect practice operations to financial outcomes, including demand forecasting, capacity, utilization, revenue, margin, labor mix, investment, and measurable efficiency gains.
  • Establish and review a balanced scorecard covering delivery quality, cycle time, backlog throughput, utilization, revenue, customer satisfaction, reuse, automation savings, adoption, and team capability.
  • Provide governance and executive oversight for strategic or high-risk engagements; resolve escalations, remove systemic blockers, and ensure durable corrective actions.
  • Drive delivery readiness by keeping methods, tools, environments, documentation, and enablement aligned to product and SaaS release cycles.
  • Support Sales and account teams with service strategy, scoping, estimates, proposals, pricing inputs, demonstrations, and executive customer conversations for complex opportunities.

Customer and Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Serve as a trusted advisor and senior escalation point for customers undertaking complex migrations, conversions, automation programs, or AI-enabled transformation.
  • Build strong working relationships with regional Professional Services teams and functional subject-matter experts to align global standards with customer and market realities.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Cloud, Support, Security, Legal, Finance, Enablement, and Sales to address platform gaps, prioritize investments, and ensure solutions can be supported at scale.
  • Develop customer evidence, case studies, metrics, and reusable lessons that strengthen adoption, pre-sales credibility, and continuous improvement across the practice.

What You Will Bring

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in professional services, consulting, enterprise software delivery, data services, engineering, or a closely related field, including significant people-leadership responsibility.
  • Demonstrated success leading global or distributed teams and building multidisciplinary capabilities across managers, technical leads, consultants, developers, and delivery practitioners.
  • Deep knowledge of complex enterprise data migration and conversion, including source-data discovery, ETL/ELT, mapping, transformation, validation, reconciliation, testing, cutover, and data-quality management.
  • Experience leading AI, software automation, or RPA portfolios, with practical knowledge of platforms such as UiPath or comparable tools and familiarity with APIs, SQL, scripting, intelligent document processing, and AI/ML-enabled workflows.
  • Proven ability to productize consulting capabilities through standardized methods, reusable assets, accelerators, reference architectures, runbooks, and enablement.
  • Strong operational and financial acumen, including utilization, revenue, margin, demand and capacity planning, labor strategy, business cases, and benefits realization.
  • Experience with Agile delivery and portfolio-management practices, including backlog prioritization, Jira or equivalent work-management platforms, and outcome-based metrics.
  • Demonstrated expertise in design thinking and product management, with the ability to apply human-centered design principles, identify customer needs, prioritize requirements, and translate innovative ideas into actionable product strategies and solutions.
  • Executive-level communication, stakeholder management, and customer-facing consulting skills; ability to simplify complex technical and operational topics and influence across organizational boundaries.
  • Sound judgment regarding data privacy, security, responsible AI, intellectual property, compliance, and risk in customer and internal delivery environments.

Not Required, but Preferred

  • Experience in higher education technology, student information systems, ERP implementations, or Ellucian Banner and Colleague environments.
  • Experience with cloud-native and agentic AI architectures, including AWS or Azure services, knowledge bases, vector search, orchestration, and secure model integration.
  • UiPath certification or equivalent automation-platform credentials.
  • Experience building and scaling a Center of Excellence, global delivery model, or nearshore capability.
  • Prior accountability for a consulting practice budget, P&L, or portfolio-level financial plan.
  • Background in process reengineering, Lean, Six Sigma, or another structured continuous-improvement discipline.

How Success Will Be Measured

  • Consistent, high-quality delivery with improved predictability, customer satisfaction, and fewer avoidable post-go-live issues.
  • Reduced migration and automation cycle times, lower delivery effort, stronger validation, and increased throughput.
  • Achievement of revenue, margin, utilization, capacity, and cost-efficiency objectives for the practices.
  • Adoption and reuse of global methods, tooling, templates, mappings, components, and other intellectual property across regions and engagements.
  • A transparent, prioritized portfolio with measurable value realization from AI and automation investments.
  • A healthy, engaged, and increasingly capable team with strong retention, succession, certification, and internal mobility.
  • Effective governance of data, AI, security, supportability, and operational risk.
  • This job description summarizes the principal responsibilities of the role and is not intended to be an exhaustive list. Responsibilities may evolve as business needs, technologies, and the Professional Services operating model change.

jobs.title: Junior Retention Strategist (Email & SMS)
jobs.excerpt: The short version You’ll be second in command of a client pod, sitting directly beside a senior Retention Strategist and learning to do their job while you’re still doing yours.
jobs.description:
The short version
You’ll be second in command of a client pod, sitting directly beside a senior Retention Strategist and learning to do their job while you’re still doing yours.
Most agency roles at this level hand you a brief and expect you to build it. This one expects you to read the brief, understand why it exists, and tell us when it’s wrong.

Why this role exists
We run client work in pods. Each pod has a Strategist who owns the thinking, the client relationship and the revenue outcome; an Activations Specialist who owns the technical build and QA in Klaviyo; plus a designer and a copywriter.
We kept hitting the same gap. The Strategist gets pulled into execution when things get busy. The Activations Specialist can execute anything but hasn’t been trained to think about why. Neither can fully cover the other.

So we’re building the seat in between.

You’re the Strategist’s right hand. When they’re on a client call, you’re moving the pod. When they’re on leave, you hold the account. When the Activations Specialist is buried, you build. You’re the person who knows enough about both sides to keep an account running without either one of them in the room.
That’s a lot of responsibility for a junior seat. It’s also the fastest way we know to make someone a strategist.

What you’ll learn here
This is the part most job posts skip, so we’ll be specific.
You’ll learn to diagnose instead of guess. Klaviyo revenue is down 20% this month. Is that a flow problem, a deliverability problem, a list fatigue problem, or is store revenue just down and email is fine? Most people at your level can’t tell those apart. You’ll learn to, on real accounts, with a senior strategist checking your reasoning.
You’ll learn what actually moves retention revenue. Flow architecture, segmentation, offer strategy, cadence. Not formatting tweaks, not sending more email.
You’ll learn to think in leverage. On any account there are twenty things you could do. Two of them matter. Picking those two is the entire job of a strategist, and it’s a skill you build by being asked the question every week until you have an answer.
You’ll learn to own a client narrative. What happened, why it happened, what we’re doing about it. Delivered clearly enough that a client trusts you in a bad month, not just a good one.
You’ll sit in gameplan reviews, standups and client calls with senior strategists from day one. You’ll be asked for your view. You’ll be wrong sometimes and told why.
Do this well and you’re running your own pod as a full Strategist inside 12 to 18 months. That’s not a vague promise. It’s the path, and we’ve moved people down it.

What you’ll actually do
Execute at a level that never needs checking. Build flows, campaigns, segments and popups in Klaviyo. Triggers, filters, conditional splits, send windows, suppression logic, UTMs. Correct the first time.
Own QA like your name is on it. Rendering across Gmail, Apple Mail and Outlook. Live links. Dynamic content resolving properly. Exclusions actually excluding. A send with an error is worse than a late send, and you’re the last line before it goes out.
Question the brief. This is the part we mean seriously. If a flow doesn’t make sense, if a segment will overlap with something already live, if the timing will cannibalise a campaign — say it before you build, not after. Executing a bad brief perfectly is still a bad outcome, and we’d rather you push back.
Read the numbers and form a view. Pull the data, then tell us what it means. “Browse abandonment RPR dropped 30% after we changed the segment” is worth more than a clean export.
Keep production honest. ClickUp current in real time. Blockers flagged the moment you see them, not the day of the deadline. Nobody should have to chase you.
Step into either seat when the pod needs it. Cover the Strategist on a call or a weekly update. Cover the build when the Activations Specialist is stretched.

Who this is for
You’re already fast in the tools. This part isn’t negotiable.

  • 2+ years hands-on in Klaviyo for an ecommerce brand or agency. Not “familiar with.” You’ve built multi-branch flows, written nested segment logic, debugged a trigger that wasn’t firing, and know exactly where Klaviyo’s date-relative filters trip people up.
  • Working knowledge of Shopify — how the integration feeds Klaviyo, what the standard events and properties are, where the data breaks.
  • Comfortable with the wider stack (reviews, subscriptions, loyalty, SMS, popups) and able to figure out a new tool without a walkthrough.
  • You want to know why, and you ask.
  • You flag what looks wrong even when it isn’t strictly yours.
  • You can explain a decision in one sentence.
  • You manage your own timelines.

You think past the ticket.

You don’t need to be the smartest person in the room. You need to be curious, accurate, and hard to rattle. We’ll teach you the rest.
This isn’t for you if: you want a pure strategy seat and expect someone else to build. In this role you build, and the building is what earns you the strategic seat.

Setup
Fully remote, full-time. A defined portfolio of ecommerce clients, a small pod you’ll work with daily, and direct access to senior strategists and managers. You will not be left to figure it out alone.

NeuroFlow CEO and West Point graduate Christopher Molaro served in the army for five years, including a tour in Iraq as a platoon leader. While pursuing his MBA at Wharton, Chris met his future co-founder Adam Pardes, and the two agreed – even the most engaging digital mental health apps in the world wouldn’t truly change the problem; only a solution that systematically integrated behavioral health into the full healthcare ecosystem could create meaningful change. And so they created NeuroFlow.

What We Do:

We pride ourselves on partnering with healthcare leaders to assist in driving better outcomes, lowering total cost of care, and making behavioral health risk more predictable and transparent. NeuroFlow exists to make sure no one who needs behavioral health support falls through the cracks.

We build more than just engaging digital health tools for self-care: we create platforms that identify population behavioral health risk early, engage individuals with acuity-specific resources, and enable care teams to make smarter and more efficient decisions. Together, NeuroFlow’s solutions arm healthcare organizations with the insights they need to overcome the systemic challenges in today’s healthcare ecosystem.

How We Do It:

The award-winning culture at NeuroFlow is one built around encouragement and daring to be great. Our core values have been displayed in our office since day one, and each team member is responsible for carrying out these values and keeping each other accountable to them. We succeed through our flexibility and agility, navigating and transforming an industry ripe for change where “no” or “can’t” is too often the default. NeuroFlow offers unique opportunities to work in a fun and challenging fast-paced environment with direct, meaningful impact on helping to close the divide between mental and physical health.

The Opportunity

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who thrives in the earliest and most exciting stages of a market. You'll own a regional book of business selling NeuroFlow's solutions directly to commercial insurance carriers — targeting CMOs, CMCOs, VP-level behavioral health leaders, and their operational, financial and technical counterparts.

Own the full sales cycle across a defined geographic territory, from initial prospecting through contract execution, for deals that typically involve multiple stakeholders and 6–12+ month sales cycles.

Lead deeply consultative discovery to surface latent pain, understand organizational priorities, and connect NeuroFlow's capabilities to the clinical, financial, operational, and technical needs of each buyer. You don't pitch — you diagnose.

Navigate complex buying committees that span behavioral health clinical leaders, care management and operations, finance, IT, and procurement. You'll build multilateral relationships and ensure NeuroFlow has champions at every relevant level.

Apply a rigorous sales methodology (MEDDIC/MEDDPICC or equivalent) to qualify opportunities, maintain forecast integrity, and drive disciplined pipeline progression. You document what you know, know what you don't, and pursue both relentlessly.

Leverage technology to sell smarter. You're a power user of your CRM and the broader sales tech stack — AI tools, engagement platforms, research tools — and you actively look for ways to create leverage in your process.

Contribute to the playbook. As an early member of the payer sales team, you'll help define what great looks like — sharing discovery frameworks, objection handling, competitive intelligence, and deal strategies that make the whole team better.

What We're Looking For

Experience & Background

  • 8+ years of enterprise sales experience, with meaningful time selling to payers
  • Track record closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals in the $500K–$2M+ range
  • Experience selling analytics, SaaS, or tech-enabled services in a payer context; behavioral health familiarity is a strong plus
  • Demonstrated success selling in early-stage or emerging markets where the category itself requires evangelism
  • Comfort with AI tools and a genuine curiosity about how emerging technology can be applied to do better, faster work

Competencies & Approach

  • Deeply discovery-oriented — you believe the quality of your questions is your primary competitive advantage
  • Fluent across buyer personas: you can hold a credible conversation with a CMO about clinical outcomes and pivot to a CFO conversation about ROI and a CIO conversation about integration
  • Practiced in MEDDIC, MEDDPICC, Challenger, or a similarly rigorous qualification and opportunity management framework — and you actually use it, not just recite it
  • Highly process-oriented: you maintain a clean, accurate pipeline, forecast with integrity, and don't let deals drift without a clear next step
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and energized by building — you can construct a point of view and a path forward in accounts where there's no established blueprint
  • Embraces technology as a force multiplier: CRM hygiene is non-negotiable, and you actively leverage AI tools, sales engagement platforms, and data sources to work smarter

Mindset

  • Intellectually curious — you read the trades, understand what's keeping payer executives up at night, and bring ideas to conversations, not just slides
  • Resilient and self-directed — you don't need a manager to tell you what to do next in a deal; you think three moves ahead
  • Humble enough to learn and confident enough to lead — you'll be shaping a market that doesn't fully exist yet, which requires both

Company Benefits:

*Applicable for full time employees

Flexible work schedule, unlimited PTO, physical and mental wellness benefits, medical coverage, parental leave, 401K, company-sponsored events, referral program, onsite gym, dog friendly office, snacks in the office, commuter benefits, onsite massages.

Every day we are working to tackle the mental health crisis in America, and in order to do that well, we need diverse voices, experiences, and perspectives at the table. As a HIPAA compliant organization
